title: Review Article: Cancer Surveillance for Early Detection of Liver Cancer in Patients with HBV Infection
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although antiviral therapy reduces cirrhosis and liver failure, HCC may still develop in patients with HBV, including in non‐cirrhotic livers. This review aimed to evaluate current HCC surveillance strategies in HBV infection, focusing on risk stratification and advances in early detection. Methods English‐language literature published in PubMed and the Cochrane Database was comprehensively reviewed. This narrative review assessed the effectiveness of HCC surveillance strategies in HBV‐infected patients, with emphasis on recent advances in early‐stage HCC detection. Results This review summarizes viral, host and environmental factors associated with HCC susceptibility and evaluates current surveillance using ultrasound with or without alpha‐fetoprotein (AFP). Surveillance eligibility should follow guideline‐defined risk criteria: patients with an estimated annual HCC risk below 0.2% generally do not require routine surveillance and should undergo periodic risk reassessment, whereas patients meeting surveillance criteria should undergo ultrasound with or without AFP every 6 months. Risk‐prediction scores can refine assessment but should be distinguished from early‐detection tests. GALAD, HES 2.0, multi‐target blood tests, and abbreviated magnetic resonance imaging are promising early‐detection approaches, but much of the supporting evidence derives from mixed‐aetiology or non‐HBV cohorts and prospective HBV‐specific validation remains limited. Conclusion A risk‐adapted approach should separate estimation of future HCC risk from surveillance and early‐detection testing. Guideline‐eligible patients should undergo surveillance every 6 months, while emerging biomarker, imaging and artificial‐intelligence approaches remain adjunctive or investigational pending further HBV‐specific validation.

source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although antiviral therapy reduces cirrhosis and liver failure, HCC may still develop in patients with HBV, including in non‐cirrhotic livers. This review aimed to evaluate current HCC surveillance strategies in HBV infection, focusing on risk stratification and advances in early detection. Methods English‐language literature published in PubMed and the Cochrane Database was comprehensively reviewed. This narrative review assessed the effectiveness of HCC surveillance strategies in HBV‐infected patients, with emphasis on recent advances in early‐stage HCC detection. Results This review summarizes viral, host and environmental factors associated with HCC susceptibility and evaluates current surveillance using ultrasound with or without alpha‐fetoprotein (AFP). Surveillance eligibility should follow guideline‐defined risk criteria: patients with an estimated annual HCC risk below 0.2% generally do not require routine surveillance and should undergo periodic risk reassessment, whereas patients meeting surveillance criteria should undergo ultrasound with or without AFP every 6 months. Risk‐prediction scores can refine assessment but should be distinguished from early‐detection tests. GALAD, HES 2.0, multi‐target blood tests, and abbreviated magnetic resonance imaging are promising early‐detection approaches, but much of the supporting evidence derives from mixed‐aetiology or non‐HBV cohorts and prospective HBV‐specific validation remains limited. Conclusion A risk‐adapted approach should separate estimation of future HCC risk from surveillance and early‐detection testing. Guideline‐eligible patients should undergo surveillance every 6 months, while emerging biomarker, imaging and artificial‐intelligence approaches remain adjunctive or investigational pending further HBV‐specific validation.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景和目的 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 感染仍然是肝细胞癌 (HCC) 的主要原因。尽管 抗病毒药物 治疗可减少肝硬化和肝衰竭,但 HBV 患者(包括非肝硬化肝脏)仍可能发展为 HCC。本综述旨在评估当前 HCC 监测 治疗 HBV 感染的策略,重点关注风险分层和早期检测的进展。方法 全面回顾 PubMed 和 Cochrane 数据库中发表的英文文献。这篇叙述性综述评估了 HCC 监测 策略在 HBV 感染患者中的有效性,重点关注早期 HCC 检测的最新进展。结果 本综述总结了与 HCC 易感性相关的病毒、宿主 和环境因素,并使用有或没有甲胎蛋白 (AFP) 的超声评估了当前的 监测。监测 资格应遵循指南定义的风险标准:估计年度 HCC 风险低于 0.2% 的患者通常不需要常规 监测,而应定期进行风险重新评估,而符合 监测 标准的患者应每 6 个月接受超声检查(伴或不伴 AFP)。风险预测分数可以完善评估,但应与早期检测测试区分开来。GALAD、HES 2.0、多目标血液检测和简化磁共振成像是有前途的早期检测方法,但许多支持证据来自混合病因学或非 HBV 队列研究,前瞻性 HBV 特异性验证仍然有限。结论 风险适应方法应将未来 HCC 风险的估计与 监测 和早期检测测试分开。符合指南资格的患者应每 6 个月接受一次 监测,而新兴的生物标志物、影像学和人工智能方法仍处于辅助或研究阶段,有待进一步的 HBV 特异性验证。

title: High Treatment Adherence Is Associated With Lower Observed HCC Risk in Patients With Chronic Hepatitis B and Cirrhosis: A Nationwide Claims‐Based Cohort Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Adherence to antiviral therapy is essential for viral suppression in chronic hepatitis B (CHB), yet its effect on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains uncertain. We examined the association between nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) adherence and HCC risk, focusing on tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) versus entecavir (ETV). Treatment‐naïve adults with CHB initiating TAF or ETV were identified from the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service, Republic of Korea. Adherence was measured using the medication possession ratio, with high adherence defined as ≥ 90%, and the primary outcome was HCC incidence. A total of 28 448 patients were included, of whom 19 001 (66.8%) showed high adherence and 9447 (33.2%) showed low adherence. In the overall cohort, HCC incidence was comparable between the high‐ and low‐adherence groups (14.89 vs. 13.76 per 1000 person‐years; IRR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.95–1.24). Among patients with claims‐defined cirrhosis, however, high adherence was associated with lower observed HCC incidence (32.92 vs. 49.59 per 1000 person‐years; IRR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.57–0.78), and this association remained significant in multivariable Cox regression (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.66–0.90) as well as in IPTW, landmark, and sensitivity analyses. In exploratory regimen‐stratified analyses, high‐adherence TAF users showed a lower observed cumulative HCC incidence than high‐adherence ETV users, whereas no significant difference was observed in the low‐adherence group. Logistic regression identified ETV use as a predictor of low adherence (OR, 2.80; 95% CI, 2.65–2.96). High adherence to antiviral therapy was associated with lower observed HCC incidence among patients with CHB and claims‐defined cirrhosis. Although this association remained evident across multiple analyses, residual confounding, treatment‐selection effects, time‐related bias, and competing‐risk issues cannot be fully excluded.

Among patients with claims‐defined cirrhosis, however, high adherence was associated with lower observed HCC incidence (32.92 vs. 49.59 per 1000 person‐years; IRR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.57–0.78), and this association remained significant in multivariable Cox regression (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.66–0.90) as well as in IPTW, landmark, and sensitivity analyses. In exploratory regimen‐stratified analyses, high‐adherence TAF users showed a lower observed cumulative HCC incidence than high‐adherence ETV users, whereas no significant difference was observed in the low‐adherence group. Logistic regression identified ETV use as a predictor of low adherence (OR, 2.80; 95% CI, 2.65–2.96). High adherence to antiviral therapy was associated with lower observed HCC incidence among patients with CHB and claims‐defined cirrhosis. Although this association remained evident across multiple analyses, residual confounding, treatment‐selection effects, time‐related bias, and competing‐risk issues cannot be fully excluded.

abstract: Based on the United Network for Organ Sharing database (9/1/2022-6/30/2024), only 59.9% liver transplant recipients were vaccinated against hepatitis B virus. The vaccination rate varied widely by region and other clinicodemographic factors. Multilevel interventions and the utilization of a more immunogenic vaccine may improve vaccination rates in this population.

title: A Markov model cost threshold analysis of potential hepatitis B virus cure regimens
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Novel treatment regimens to achieve functional cure (FC) of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) may soon be available. We aimed to evaluate treatment cost-effectiveness thresholds for a potential cure regimen in the U.S. and China using a Markov model, with long-term nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) treatment as reference. METHODS: We simulated disease progression comparing achieving FC defined as HBsAg loss and unquantifiable HBV DNA 24 weeks off treatment with a novel therapeutic regimen to long-term NUC treatment. Cost-effectiveness thresholds for FC of CHB, incorporating various anticipated success rates for FC, incidence rates of major liver outcomes including hepatocellular carcinoma post-FC, health utility values, and medical costs, were estimated. RESULTS: The base case was a 50-year-old man with hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg)-negative non-cirrhotic CHB and NUC-suppressed HBV DNA ≥1year. Compared to long-term NUC, a 30% effective FC regimen would yield 17.18 and 16.14 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and 0.30 and 0.57 QALYs gained per patient in the U.S. and China, respectively. With an HCC annual incidence rate of 0.1% after FC, a FC regimen could be cost-effective at a one-time treatment cost under the threshold of USD46,642 in the U.S., and USD13,008 in China. The cost-effectiveness threshold increases with higher FC rates, younger patients, and increasing medical costs, but may be lower in women. DISCUSSION: A Markov model-based cost-effectiveness analysis demonstrates that CHB cure regimen with 30% FC in aforementioned base case could be cost-effective at a threshold of USD46,642 in the U.S. and USD13,008 in China.

METHODS: We simulated disease progression comparing achieving FC defined as HBsAg loss and unquantifiable HBV DNA 24 weeks off treatment with a novel therapeutic regimen to long-term NUC treatment. Cost-effectiveness thresholds for FC of CHB, incorporating various anticipated success rates for FC, incidence rates of major liver outcomes including hepatocellular carcinoma post-FC, health utility values, and medical costs, were estimated. RESULTS: The base case was a 50-year-old man with hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg)-negative non-cirrhotic CHB and NUC-suppressed HBV DNA ≥1year. Compared to long-term NUC, a 30% effective FC regimen would yield 17.18 and 16.14 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and 0.30 and 0.57 QALYs gained per patient in the U.S. and China, respectively. With an HCC annual incidence rate of 0.1% after FC, a FC regimen could be cost-effective at a one-time treatment cost under the threshold of USD46,642 in the U.S., and USD13,008 in China. The cost-effectiveness threshold increases with higher FC rates, younger patients, and increasing medical costs, but may be lower in women. DISCUSSION: A Markov model-based cost-effectiveness analysis demonstrates that CHB cure regimen with 30% FC in aforementioned base case could be cost-effective at a threshold of USD46,642 in the U.S. and USD13,008 in China.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness thresholds for a potential hepatitis B virus (HBV) cure regimen using a Markov model. The research focuses on comparing a 30% effective functional cure (FC) regimen with long-term nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) treatment in the U.S. and China. The base case involves a 50-year-old man with HBeAg-negative non-cirrhotic chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and NUC-suppressed HBV DNA ≥1 year. The results indicate that the FC regimen could yield 0.30 and 0.57 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) gained per patient in the U.S. and China, respectively, and may be cost-effective under specific thresholds. The findings suggest that cost-effectiveness depends on factors such as FC rates, patient age, and medical costs. However, the study has limitations due to its reliance on simulated data and assumptions, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 新型治疗方案以实现功能性治愈(功能性治愈)的慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)可能即将问世。本研究旨在利用马尔可夫模型,评估治疗在美中两国潜在治愈方案中的成本效益阈值,以长期核苷(酸)类似物(NUC)治疗作为参考。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究模拟了疾病进展,比较了以HBsAg消失和HBV DNA不可量化作为功能性治愈(FC)标准的治疗方案在24周后与新型治疗方案的效果,以及与长期使用NUC治疗的对比。基线案例为一名50岁的男性,患有乙型肝炎e抗原(HBeAg)阴性、非肝硬化的慢性乙型肝炎(CHB),且HBV DNA已被NUC抑制≥1年。
elements_zh.methods: 功能性治愈慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)的成本效果阈值,结合了功能性治愈(FC)的各种预期成功率、功能性治愈后主要肝脏结局(包括肝细胞癌)的发生率、健康效用值以及医疗成本,通过马尔可夫模型进行了估算。
elements_zh.main_results: 一种30%有效的FC方案在美国和中国分别可获得17.18和16.14个质量调整生命年(QALYs),每位患者分别获得0.30和0.57个QALYs的增益。成本效果阈值随着更高的FC率、更年轻的患者和医疗成本的增加而上升,但在女性中可能较低。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: A Markov model-based cost-effectiveness analysis demonstrates that CHB cure regimen with 30% FC in aforementioned base case could be cost-effective at a threshold of USD46,642 in the U.S. and USD13,008 in China.
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为美国和中国潜在的乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)治愈方案的成本效益决策提供信息,特别是针对HBeAg阴性、非肝硬化的慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者以及接受核苷(酸)类似物(NUC)治疗且HBV DNA被抑制≥1年的患者。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于其依赖预期成功率和发病率率来评估肝病结果,这些数据可能无法反映真实世界的情况。由于其基于模拟数据和假设,证据强度为中等。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Novel treatment regimens to achieve functional cure (FC) of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) may soon be available. The study aimed to evaluate treatment cost-effectiveness thresholds for a potential cure regimen in the U.S. and China using a Markov model, with long-term nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) treatment as reference.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study simulated disease progression comparing achieving FC defined as HBsAg loss and unquantifiable HBV DNA 24 weeks off treatment with a novel therapeutic regimen to long-term NUC treatment. The base case was a 50-year-old man with hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg)-negative non-cirrhotic CHB and NUC-suppressed HBV DNA ≥1 year.
analysis_en.methods: Cost-effectiveness thresholds for FC of CHB, incorporating various anticipated success rates for FC, incidence rates of major liver outcomes including hepatocellular carcinoma post-FC, health utility values, and medical costs, were estimated using a Markov model.
analysis_en.main_results: A 30% effective FC regimen would yield 17.18 and 16.14 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and 0.30 and 0.57 QALYs gained per patient in the U.S. and China, respectively. The cost-effectiveness threshold increases with higher FC rates, younger patients, and increasing medical costs, but may be lower in women.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: A Markov model-based cost-effectiveness analysis demonstrates that CHB cure regimen with 30% FC in aforementioned base case could be cost-effective at a threshold of USD46,642 in the U.S. and USD13,008 in China.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform cost-effectiveness decisions for potential HBV cure regimens in the U.S. and China, particularly for patients with HBeAg-negative non-cirrhotic CHB and NUC-suppressed HBV DNA ≥1 year.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on anticipated success rates and incidence rates for liver outcomes, which may not reflect real-world scenarios. The evidence strength is moderate as it is based on simulated data and assumptions.

title_zh: 一种基于马尔可夫模型的潜在乙型肝炎病毒治愈方案成本阈值分析
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Novel treatment regimens to achieve functional cure (FC) of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) may soon be available. We aimed to evaluate treatment cost-effectiveness thresholds for a potential cure regimen in the U.S. and China using a Markov model, with long-term nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) treatment as reference. METHODS: We simulated disease progression comparing achieving FC defined as HBsAg loss and unquantifiable HBV DNA 24 weeks off treatment with a novel therapeutic regimen to long-term NUC treatment. Cost-effectiveness thresholds for FC of CHB, incorporating various anticipated success rates for FC, incidence rates of major liver outcomes including hepatocellular carcinoma post-FC, health utility values, and medical costs, were estimated. RESULTS: The base case was a 50-year-old man with hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg)-negative non-cirrhotic CHB and NUC-suppressed HBV DNA ≥1year. Compared to long-term NUC, a 30% effective FC regimen would yield 17.18 and 16.14 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and 0.30 and 0.57 QALYs gained per patient in the U.S. and China, respectively. With an HCC annual incidence rate of 0.1% after FC, a FC regimen could be cost-effective at a one-time treatment cost under the threshold of USD46,642 in the U.S., and USD13,008 in China. The cost-effectiveness threshold increases with higher FC rates, younger patients, and increasing medical costs, but may be lower in women. DISCUSSION: A Markov model-based cost-effectiveness analysis demonstrates that CHB cure regimen with 30% FC in aforementioned base case could be cost-effective at a threshold of USD46,642 in the U.S. and USD13,008 in China.

title: Impact of resolved hepatitis B virus infection on clinical outcomes in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a supplementary analysis of JCOG0601
abstract: The impact of resolved hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, defined as pretreatment hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) negativity with antibody to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc) positivity, on the clinical characteristics and outcomes of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) remains unclear. JCOG0601 was a randomized phase II/III trial showing no improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) with dose-dense rituximab plus CHOP in previously untreated DLBCL. This supplementary analysis of JCOG0601 evaluated whether baseline anti-HBc positivity affects PFS and overall survival (OS) in patients with HBsAg-negative DLBCL treated with rituximab-containing CHOP-based therapy. Among 406 eligible patients randomly assigned in JCOG0601, 405 with available baseline HBV serologic data were included. Baseline characteristics and outcomes were compared according to anti-HBc status. Of the 405 patients, 87 were anti-HBc-positive and 318 were anti-HBc-negative. Anti-HBc-positive patients were older than anti-HBc-negative patients (median age, 63 vs. 61 years; p = 0.008). No significant differences in PFS or OS were observed between the two groups (3-year PFS, 78% vs. 81%; 3-year OS, 90% vs. HBV reactivation occurred in five anti-HBc-positive patients. Baseline anti-HBc positivity was more common in older patients but was not associated with inferior outcomes in HBsAg-negative DLBCL treated with rituximab-containing CHOP-based therapy.Clinical trial registration: JCOG0601 was registered in the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCTs031180139, date of registration; February 20, 2019).

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of resolved hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection on clinical outcomes in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). It is a supplementary analysis of the JCOG0601 trial, which evaluated rituximab-containing CHOP-based therapy in previously untreated DLBCL. The study found that anti-HBc positivity was more common in older patients but did not correlate with inferior progression-free survival (PFS) or overall survival (OS). HBV reactivation occurred in five anti-HBc-positive patients, but no significant differences in outcomes were observed between the groups. The findings suggest that resolved HBV infection does not negatively affect clinical outcomes in HBsAg-negative DLBCL patients. However, the study's limitations include its supplementary nature and the potential for confounding factors, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Intracellular Zn2+ levels regulate susceptibility to hepatitis B virus infection by modulating NTCP-mediated viral entry.
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a significant global health challenge and is a leading cause of chronic liver diseases, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Although nucleos(t)ide analogs and interferon-based therapies suppress viral replication, they do not eliminate the viral reservoir, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies. HBV utilizes the sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP) as a key receptor for hepatocyte entry; however, the underlying mechanisms governing this process remain incompletely understood. In this study, we demonstrate that intracellular Zn 2+ levels, regulated by zinc transporter 1 (ZnT1), also known as solute carrier family 30 member 1 (SLC30A1), serve as critical modulators of HBV entry. Zinc supplementation significantly reduced both HBV and hepatitis D virus infection in NTCP-expressing hepatocytes without affecting post-entry replication steps. Knockout or knockdown of SLC30A1 led to intracellular Zn 2+ accumulation and impaired HBV infection, effects reversed by re-expression of functional SLC30A1 or treatment with the Zn 2+ chelator TPEN. Mechanistically, elevated Zn 2+ levels disrupted NTCP-mediated HBV/HDV internalization and bile acid uptake, implicating Zn 2+ in the regulation of receptor activity. RNA sequencing analysis further revealed transcriptional reprogramming of metabolic and bile acid-associated pathways in Zn 2+ -treated cells. Collectively, these findings reveal a role for intracellular zinc homeostasis in regulating HBV entry and implicate the SLC30A1-Zn2+-NTCP axis in this process.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This study aimed to investigate the role of intracellular Zn2+ levels in regulating HBV entry by modulating NTCP-mediated viral entry. The research was conducted using NTCP-expressing hepatocytes and involved RNA sequencing analysis.
analysis.methods: The study utilized RNA sequencing to analyze metabolic and bile acid-associated pathways in Zn2+-treated cells. Additionally, knockout or knockdown of SLC30A1 and treatment with the Zn2+ chelator TPEN were employed to assess the effects on HBV infection.
analysis.main_results: Zinc supplementation significantly reduced both HBV and hepatitis D virus infection in NTCP-expressing hepatocytes without affecting post-entry replication steps. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Knockout or knockdown of SLC30A1 led to intracellular Zn2+ accumulation and impaired HBV infection, effects reversed by re-expression of functional SLC30A1 or treatment with the Zn2+ chelator TPEN. These findings reveal a role for intracellular zinc homeostasis in regulating HBV entry and implicate the SLC30A1-Zn2+-NTCP axis in this process.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting intracellular Zn2+ levels could be a novel therapeutic strategy for HBV infection. This could have implications for the development of new treatments and improve patient outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of in vitro models, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions. Additionally, the sample size and specific host populations were not detailed, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate.

elements_en.study_design_and_population: This study aimed to investigate the role of intracellular Zn2+ levels in regulating HBV entry by modulating NTCP-mediated viral entry. The research was conducted using NTCP-expressing hepatocytes and involved RNA sequencing analysis.
elements_en.methods: The study utilized RNA sequencing to analyze metabolic and bile acid-associated pathways in Zn2+-treated cells. Additionally, knockout or knockdown of SLC30A1 and treatment with the Zn2+ chelator TPEN were employed to assess the effects on HBV infection.
elements_en.main_results: Zinc supplementation significantly reduced both HBV and hepatitis D virus infection in NTCP-expressing hepatocytes without affecting post-entry replication steps. Mechanistically, elevated Zn2+ levels disrupted NTCP-mediated HBV/HDV internalization and bile acid uptake, implicating Zn2+ in the regulation of receptor activity.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Knockout or knockdown of SLC30A1 led to intracellular Zn2+ accumulation and impaired HBV infection, effects reversed by re-expression of functional SLC30A1 or treatment with the Zn2+ chelator TPEN. These findings reveal a role for intracellular zinc homeostasis in regulating HBV entry and implicate the SLC30A1-Zn2+-NTCP axis in this process.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting intracellular Zn2+ levels could be a novel therapeutic strategy for HBV infection. This could have implications for the development of new treatments and improve patient outcomes.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of in vitro models, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions. Additionally, the sample size and specific host populations were not detailed, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染仍然是全球重要的健康挑战,并是导致慢性肝病(包括肝硬化和肝细胞癌)的主要原因。尽管核苷(酸)类似物和基于干扰素的治疗可以抑制病毒复制,但它们无法清除病毒储存宿主,凸显了开发新型治疗策略的必要性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究旨在通过调节NTCP介导的病毒入侵来探讨细胞内Zn2+水平在调控HBV入侵中的作用。研究使用了表达NTCP的肝细胞,并涉及RNA测序分析。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究利用RNA测序分析了Zn2+处理细胞中的代谢和胆汁酸相关通路。此外,还通过敲除或敲减SLC30A1以及使用Zn2+螯合剂TPEN结合治疗来评估其对HBV感染的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 补充锌显著降低了NTCP表达肝细胞中HBV和肝炎D病毒的感染,而不会影响入侵后的复制步骤。机制上,Zn2+水平升高破坏了NTCP介导的HBV/HDV内化和胆汁酸摄取,表明Zn2+在调节受体活性中起作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 敲除或敲减SLC30A1导致细胞内Zn2+积累并损害HBV感染,这些效应可通过重新表达功能性SLC30A1或与Zn2+螯合剂TPEN结合的治疗逆转。这些发现表明细胞内锌稳态在调控HBV入侵中起作用,并暗示了SLC30A1-Zn2+-NTCP轴在此过程中的作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,针对细胞内Zn2+水平可能是一种治疗HBV感染的新策略。这可能对开发新的治疗并改善患者预后产生影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了体外模型,这可能无法完全反映体内条件。此外,样本量和特定宿主人群未详细说明,这可能影响结果的普遍性。证据强度为中等。

title_zh: 细胞内Zn2+水平通过调节NTCP介导的病毒入侵来调控对乙型肝炎病毒感染的易感性。
source_body_en: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a significant global health challenge and is a leading cause of chronic liver diseases, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Although nucleos(t)ide analogs and interferon-based therapies suppress viral replication, they do not eliminate the viral reservoir, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies. HBV utilizes the sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP) as a key receptor for hepatocyte entry; however, the underlying mechanisms governing this process remain incompletely understood. In this study, we demonstrate that intracellular Zn 2+ levels, regulated by zinc transporter 1 (ZnT1), also known as solute carrier family 30 member 1 (SLC30A1), serve as critical modulators of HBV entry. Zinc supplementation significantly reduced both HBV and hepatitis D virus infection in NTCP-expressing hepatocytes without affecting post-entry replication steps. Knockout or knockdown of SLC30A1 led to intracellular Zn 2+ accumulation and impaired HBV infection, effects reversed by re-expression of functional SLC30A1 or treatment with the Zn 2+ chelator TPEN. Mechanistically, elevated Zn 2+ levels disrupted NTCP-mediated HBV/HDV internalization and bile acid uptake, implicating Zn 2+ in the regulation of receptor activity. RNA sequencing analysis further revealed transcriptional reprogramming of metabolic and bile acid-associated pathways in Zn 2+ -treated cells. Collectively, these findings reveal a role for intracellular zinc homeostasis in regulating HBV entry and implicate the SLC30A1-Zn2+-NTCP axis in this process.
abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染仍然是一个重大的全球健康挑战,是包括肝硬化和肝细胞癌在内的慢性肝病的主要病因。尽管核苷(酸)类似物和基于干扰素的治疗可以抑制病毒复制,但它们并不能清除病毒,这凸显了开发新型治疗策略的必要性。HBV利用钠胆酸共转运蛋白(NTCP)作为肝细胞进入的关键受体;然而,调控这一过程的潜在机制仍不完全清楚。在这项研究中,我们证明了细胞内锌离子(Zn 2+)水平,由锌转运蛋白1(ZnT1),也称为溶质载体家族30成员1(SLC30A1)所调控,是HBV进入的重要调节因子。补充锌显著降低了在表达NTCP的肝细胞中HBV和肝炎D病毒的感染,而不会影响进入后的复制步骤。敲除或敲减SLC30A1导致细胞内锌离子积累并损害HBV感染,这些效应可通过重新表达功能性SLC30A1或治疗与锌离子螯合剂TPEN逆转。从机制上看,锌离子水平升高破坏了NTCP介导的HBV/HDV内化和胆汁酸摄取,表明锌离子在调控受体活性中起作用。RNA测序分析进一步揭示了在锌离子处理的细胞中,代谢和胆汁酸相关通路的转录重编程。综上所述,这些发现表明细胞内锌稳态在调控HBV进入中起作用,并提示SLC30A1-Zn2+-NTCP轴参与这一过程。

title: Neurological Complications of Oncogenic Viruses: Mechanisms, Clinical Manifestations, and Emerging Insights.
abstract: Oncogenic viruses are widely recognized for their pivotal role in malignant transformation; however, their capacity to induce neurological disorders has received comparatively less attention. Increasing evidence indicates that several oncogenic viruses, including human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1), human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), are associated with a broad spectrum of neurological complications involving both the central and peripheral nervous systems. These manifestations arise through diverse mechanisms, including direct viral neuroinvasion, persistent infection, immune-mediated tissue injury, chronic neuroinflammation, and disruption of neurovascular integrity. Moreover, virus-induced molecular alterations, such as oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic remodelling, and aberrant cytokine signalling, contribute t neuronal dysfunction and disease progression. In this review, we critically examine the current understanding of the neurological complications associated with major oncogenic viruses by integrating evidence from molecular, experimental, and clinical studies. We first discuss the general mechanisms by which viral infections induce neurological injury, highlighting pathways shared among neurotropic and non-neurotropic viruses. We then summarise the neurological manifestations and virus-specific pathogenic mechanisms associated with each oncogenic virus, emphasising both common and distinct molecular pathways underlying neuropathogenesis. Finally, we address current diagnostic challenges, emerging biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies while identifying critical knowledge gaps that limit causal interpretation and clinical translation. A comprehensive understanding of the complex interactions between oncogenic viruses, the immune system, and the nervous system will facilitate earlier diagnosis, improve patient management, and support the development of targeted therapeutic approaches for virus-associated neurological disorders.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the neurological complications linked to hepatitis B virus (HBV), focusing on its mechanisms of action, clinical manifestations, and the challenges in diagnosis and treatment. The evidence highlights that HBV can induce neurological disorders through pathways such as direct neuroinvasion, immune-mediated injury, and molecular alterations. The review integrates findings from molecular, experimental, and clinical studies to provide a comprehensive understanding of HBV's impact on the nervous system. Despite these insights, gaps remain in causal interpretation and clinical translation, necessitating further research. The implications of this understanding include the potential for earlier diagnosis, improved patient management, and the development of targeted therapies for HBV-associated neurological conditions.

title_zh: 致癌病毒的神经并发症:机制、临床表现和新见解。
source_body_en: Oncogenic viruses are widely recognized for their pivotal role in malignant transformation; however, their capacity to induce neurological disorders has received comparatively less attention. Increasing evidence indicates that several oncogenic viruses, including human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1), human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), are associated with a broad spectrum of neurological complications involving both the central and peripheral nervous systems. These manifestations arise through diverse mechanisms, including direct viral neuroinvasion, persistent infection, immune-mediated tissue injury, chronic neuroinflammation, and disruption of neurovascular integrity. Moreover, virus-induced molecular alterations, such as oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic remodelling, and aberrant cytokine signalling, contribute t neuronal dysfunction and disease progression. In this review, we critically examine the current understanding of the neurological complications associated with major oncogenic viruses by integrating evidence from molecular, experimental, and clinical studies. We first discuss the general mechanisms by which viral infections induce neurological injury, highlighting pathways shared among neurotropic and non-neurotropic viruses. We then summarise the neurological manifestations and virus-specific pathogenic mechanisms associated with each oncogenic virus, emphasising both common and distinct molecular pathways underlying neuropathogenesis. Finally, we address current diagnostic challenges, emerging biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies while identifying critical knowledge gaps that limit causal interpretation and clinical translation. A comprehensive understanding of the complex interactions between oncogenic viruses, the immune system, and the nervous system will facilitate earlier diagnosis, improve patient management, and support the development of targeted therapeutic approaches for virus-associated neurological disorders.
abstract_zh: 致癌病毒因其在恶性转化中的关键作用而被广泛认可。然而,它们引起神经系统疾病的能力相对较少受到关注。越来越多的证据表明,多种致癌病毒,包括人 T 细胞白血病病毒 1 型 (HTLV-1)、人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV)、乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV)、丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 和卡波西肉瘤相关疱疹病毒 (KSHV),与涉及中枢和周围神经系统的广泛神经系统并发症有关。这些表现是通过多种机制产生的,包括直接病毒神经侵袭、持续感染、免疫介导的组织损伤、慢性神经炎症和神经血管完整性破坏。此外,病毒诱导的分子改变,如氧化应激、线粒体功能障碍、表观遗传重塑和异常的细胞因子信号传导,会导致神经元功能障碍和疾病进展。在这篇综述中,我们通过整合分子、实验和临床研究的证据,批判性地研究了目前对与主要致癌病毒相关的神经并发症的理解。我们首先讨论病毒感染引起神经损伤的一般机制,强调嗜神经病毒和非嗜神经病毒之间共享的途径。然后,我们总结了与每种致癌病毒相关的神经学表现和病毒特异性致病机制,强调神经发病机制中常见和独特的分子途径。最后,我们解决当前的诊断挑战、新兴生物标志物和治疗策略,同时确定限制因果解释和临床转化的关键知识差距。全面了解致癌病毒、免疫系统和神经系统之间复杂的相互作用将有助于早期 诊断,改善患者管理,并支持开发针对病毒相关神经系统疾病的靶向治疗方法。

title: Association Between EBV Lytic Replication and Liver Injury in Patients With HBeAg‐Negative Chronic HBV Infection
abstract: ABSTRACT The present study aims to characterize the impact of Epstein‐Barr virus (EBV) lytic replication on liver disease in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. We retrospectively enrolled 261 patients with HBeAg‐negative chronic HBV infection who were admitted to Zhongnan Hospital between 2019 and 2025. Plasma levels of HBV‐DNA, EBV‐DNA, and liver function parameters were collected. Patients were grouped based on their viral DNA status, and the association between viral DNA status and liver function was evaluated. Compared to the HBV‐DNA‐negative group, HBV‐DNA‐positivity was significantly associated with aggravated hepatic injury, as evidenced by elevated ALT, AST, lymphocyte count, and fibrosis scores (APRI and FIB‐4). Notably, regardless of HBV‐DNA status or the stage of liver disease (CHB or LC), EBV‐DNA‐positivity was consistently associated with significantly lower plasma albumin (Alb) levels and albumin‐to‐globulin (A/G) ratio compared to EBV‐DNA‐negative patients. The reduction in the A/G ratio was attributable to decreased Alb levels rather than to elevated globulin (Glb) levels. These results suggest that EBV lytic replication was associated with hypoalbuminemia in this study. Circulating EBV‐DNA status holds promise as a potential biomarker for monitoring disease progression, or assessing disease severity in patients with chronic HBV infection.

title: White Blood Cell to HDL ‐C Ratio and Sarcopenia: A Dual‐Cohort Analysis Including Exploratory Insights on Hepatitis B History
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Sarcopenia, driven by inflammation and lipid dysregulation, lacks inexpensive screening tools. The white blood cell to HDL‐C ratio (WHR) integrates these pathways, but its utility for sarcopenia screening remains unvalidated. Objective This study evaluated the WHR‐sarcopenia association in dual cohorts, validated it using machine learning, and explored potential effect modification of hepatitis B virus (HBV) status. Methods We analyzed 10 131 NHANES (2011–2018) and 7872 KNHANES (2010–2011) adults. Sarcopenia was defined via DXA using FNIH/AWGS criteria. Weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and machine learning (LASSO, XGBoost) were applied. Results Higher ln(WHR) was independently associated with sarcopenia in NHANES (adjusted OR = 2.50; 95% CI: 2.01–3.10) and consistently validated in KNHANES (OR = 1.85; 95% CI: 1.49–2.29). WHR ranked among the top predictive features across machine learning models. Exploratory stratified analysis suggests that the association between ln(WHR) and sarcopenia appears to be stronger in the HBV‐exposed subgroup. However, although the formal interaction test was not significant ( p = 0.270), these findings are hypothesis‐generating results. Conclusion WHR, a cost‐free routine metric, is robustly linked to sarcopenia. Integrating it into geriatric assessments could facilitate early high‐risk identification for timely interventions, while exploratory findings suggesting a possible modifying role of HBV history require prospective validation.

title: Point of Care Diagnostics for Hepatitis B and C in Low-resource Settings: A Narrative Review
abstract: Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) and Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) continue to be major public health challenge especially in Low- and MiddleIncome Countries (LMICs), with poor laboratory capacity and the ability to detect the disease earlier and contribute to its management. Proper and timely diagnosis is crucial for clinical intervention and global elimination. The present narrative review explores the potential for the use of Point-Of-Care (POC) testing to enhance the testing of HBV and HCV in low-resource settings. Peer-reviewed literature, global health reports, and grey literature were reviewed to assess the state of the art of POC technologies, diagnostic performance, and implementation in resource-limited settings, as well as new developments. Existing challenges and future opportunities for improving access to timely and effective HBV and HCV diagnosis are also pointed out. New technologies and features, such as mobile healthcare integration, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered interpretation, and self-testing, enhance their capabilities. There are still areas of challenge, including uneven policy adoption, supply chain issues, and social stigma, that make it difficult to scale. POC diagnostics have the potential to accelerate hepatitis elimination by improving access to rapid testing. Their successful implementation requires strengthened health systems, trained healthcare workers, and integration into existing healthcare services.
journal: JOURNAL OF CLINICAL AND DIAGNOSTIC RESEARCH

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review focuses on the role of Point-Of-Care (POC) diagnostics in addressing the public health challenges posed by Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) in low-resource settings. The review highlights the importance of timely diagnosis for effective clinical intervention and global elimination efforts. It explores the potential of POC technologies to enhance testing capabilities, particularly in Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs), where laboratory infrastructure is limited. The review also identifies key challenges, such as uneven policy adoption, supply chain issues, and social stigma, which hinder the scalability of POC diagnostics. Furthermore, it emphasizes the need for strengthened health systems, trained healthcare workers, and integration into existing services for successful implementation. The review concludes that while POC diagnostics offer promising opportunities, further research and policy development are required to overcome current limitations and improve access to HBV diagnosis.

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决目前缺乏可靠方法预测慢性乙型肝炎患者对治疗反应的问题,因为长期抗病毒治疗可以逆转肝纤维化,但并非所有患者都能实现逆转。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本观点综述讨论了机器学习在改善慢性乙型肝炎患者纤维化逆转预测方面的潜力,重点关注临床工具在捕捉动态纤维化过程方面的局限性。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者回顾了机器学习如何应用于分析影像数据、整合临床和病理数据,并通过在抗病毒治疗期间进行连续测量来预测患者对治疗的反应。
analysis_zh.main_results: 机器学习在三个领域已显示出早期但有希望的结果:定量影像分析、临床和病理数据的多模态整合,以及基于连续测量的动态预测患者对治疗的反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释认为,机器学习的最大价值在于补充现有工具,特别是在识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面,而不是取代它们。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,机器学习可能有助于提高慢性乙型肝炎治疗的功能性治愈率,并优化个性化治疗策略,从而改善纤维化逆转的预测能力并指导临床决策。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 目前的证据受到限制,因为大多数现有模型都是基于小规模、单一中心的回顾性数据,这可能影响其普适性,需要前瞻性多中心验证。

title: Evaluation of the immunogenicity of hepatitis B vaccination in hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients vaccinated with a hexavalent vaccine compared with patients vaccinated with a combined hepatitis A and B vaccine
abstract: BACKGROUND: In 2020, the Catalan Department of Health recommended a pediatric hexavalent vaccine for adult hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) recipients. Previously, patients at our center received a combined hepatitis A + B vaccine with double the hepatitis B antigen content. The immunogenicity of the hexavalent formulation in this population remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: To compare immunogenicity of two hepatitis B vaccination strategies in adult HSCT recipients and identify predictors of response. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including adult HSCT recipients vaccinated between 2017 and 2023 in a tertiary hospital in Barcelona. Patients received hepatitis A + B vaccine (2017-2019) or hexavalent vaccine (2020-2023). Seroprotection was defined as HBsAb ≥10 IU/mL one month after the third dose. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with seroresponse. RESULTS: A total of 331 patients were included (median age 54.6 years; 42.3% female). Seroprotection rates were higher with the hexavalent vaccine compared to hepatitis A + B (70.1% vs. Median HBsAb titers were higher but not statistically significant (668 vs. 375 IU/mL; p = 0.261) in the hexavalent group. In multivariate analysis, hexavalent vaccination (OR 4.27, 95% CI 2.88-6.36) and pre-HSCT seroprotection (OR 9.36, 95% CI 5.46-16.03) were associated with higher response. Tacrolimus use and multiple myeloma were associated with lower response. CONCLUSIONS: Despite lower antigen content, the hexavalent vaccine was associated with significantly higher seroprotection in adult HSCT recipients. Pre-existing protective HBsAb titers enhanced response, whereas tacrolimus exposure and multiple myeloma were associated with reduced immunogenicity.

elements_zh.main_results: Seroprotection rates were higher with the hexavalent vaccine compared to hepatitis A + B (70.1% vs. Median HBsAb titers were higher but not statistically significant (668 vs. 375 IU/mL; p = 0.261) in the hexavalent group. elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释称,尽管六联疫苗疫苗的抗原含量较低,但其在成年HSCT受者中与显著更高的血清保护相关。他们确定了既往保护性HBsAb滴度作为免疫应答的预测因素,同时指出他克莫司暴露和多发性骨髓瘤与免疫原性降低相关。

title: Prognostic value of Glasgow prognostic score in patients with advanced hepatitis-B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma undergoing hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy combined with lenvatinib and toripalimab.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the Glasgow Prognostic Score (GPS) in predicting prognosis in patients with advanced hepatitis-B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) who are undergoing hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) combined with lenvatinib and toripalimab therapy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, patients with advanced HBV-HCC who received treatment with HAIC combined with lenvatinib and toripalimab from March 2019 to November 2021 were analyzed. The patients were divided into two groups based on GPS, and propensity score matching (PSM) was used to assess progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) in both groups. RESULTS: Of the 58 patients, 37 were included in the study. Thirteen patients were in the GPS score 0 group and 24 in the GPS score 1 group. After PSM, eight pairs were selected. Patients in the GPS score 0 group had significantly longer median PFS before (10.2 versus 4.3 months, P = 0.009) and after PSM (5.6 versus 1.9 months, P = 0.026). Similarly, OS was significantly longer in the GPS score 0 group before (32.0 versus 9.7 months, P < 0.001) and after PSM (32.0 versus 8.6 months, P < 0.001). GPS was an independent prognostic factor for OS, with borderline significance for PFS. In addition, tumor number was identified as an independent prognostic factor for PFS. CONCLUSION: This exploratory study provides preliminary evidence that GPS may serve as a prognostic factor for patients with advanced HBV-related HCC who were receiving a triple-combination therapy, requiring further validation in larger cohorts.
journal: Journal of cancer research and therapeutics

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the Glasgow Prognostic Score (GPS) as a prognostic tool for patients with advanced hepatitis-B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) undergoing hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) combined with lenvatinib and toripalimab. A single-center retrospective analysis of 58 patients, with 37 included in the study, divided them into GPS score 0 and 1 groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to compare progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Results showed that patients in the GPS score 0 group had significantly longer median PFS (10.2 vs. 4.3 months, P = 0.009) and OS (32.0 vs. 9.7 months, P < 0.001) before and after PSM. GPS was an independent prognostic factor for OS, with borderline significance for PFS. Tumor number was also identified as an independent prognostic factor for PFS. The findings suggest GPS may be useful in predicting outcomes for patients with advanced HBV-related HCC on triple-combination therapy, though further validation in larger cohorts is needed. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估格拉斯哥预后评分(GPS)在预测接受肝动脉灌注化疗(HAIC)联合仑伐替尼和拓扑替康治疗的晚期乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌(HBV-HCC)患者预后中的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为单中心回顾性研究,分析了2019年3月至2021年11月期间接受治疗治疗的晚期HBV-HCC患者。根据GPS将患者分为两组,并采用倾向评分匹配(PSM)方法评估两组患者的无进展生存期(PFS)和总生存期(OS)。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究采用倾向评分匹配(PSM)方法,对根据格拉斯哥预后评分(GPS)分组的患者进行无进展生存期(PFS)和总生存期(OS)的评估。
elements_zh.main_results: 在58名患者中,有37名被纳入研究。其中13名患者属于GPS评分0组,24名属于GPS评分1组。PSM后选取了8对患者。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在PSM前,GPS评分0组患者的中位无进展生存期显著长于GPS评分1组(10.2个月 vs 4.3个月,P = 0.009);PSM后,GPS评分0组患者的中位无进展生存期仍显著长于GPS评分1组(5.6个月 vs 1.9个月,P = 0.026)。同样,GPS评分0组患者的总生存期在PSM前(32.0个月 vs 9.7个月,P < 0.001)和PSM后(32.0个月 vs 8.6个月,P < 0.001)均显著更长。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: GPS被确定为总生存期(OS)的独立预后因素,对无进展生存期(PFS)具有边缘显著性。此外,肿瘤数量被确定为无进展生存期(PFS)的独立预后因素。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这项探索性研究提供了初步证据,表明GPS可能作为接受三联疗法的晚期乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌(HBV-HCC)患者的预后因素,需要在更大规模的队列研究研究中进一步验证。

title: Systemic Inflammation and the Persistence of Vaccine-Induced Hepatitis B Immunity in Healthcare Workers
abstract: BACKGROUND The long-term persistence of hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs) levels varies among individuals, and the role of systemic inflammation remains unclear. This study evaluated the relationship between anti-HBs antibody levels and systemic inflammatory markers in healthcare workers. MATERIAL AND METHODS This longitudinal observational study with a retrospective component included 583 healthcare workers who underwent routine occupational health screening between 2023 and 2025. Anti-HBs levels at 2 time points were analyzed together with C-reactive protein (CRP) level, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and systemic inflammation response index. Nonparametric and correlation analyses were performed. RESULTS Anti-HBs levels decreased significantly between baseline and follow-up (Hodges-Lehmann estimate: -23.00 mIU/mL, 95% CI: -27.60 to -18.93; P<0.001). No significant associations were observed between antibody levels and sex, smoking status, or the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and systemic inflammation response index. In contrast, CRP positivity was associated with lower anti-HBs levels at the second measurement; however, no association was observed between CRP and longitudinal change in anti-HBs levels. Higher anti-HBs levels were observed among physicians and healthcare workers in the very high occupational biological-risk group, whereas age showed a weak negative correlation with antibody levels. CONCLUSIONS CRP showed a weak cross-sectional association with lower anti-HBs levels at the second measurement, whereas no association was observed between CRP or the other inflammatory indices and longitudinal change in anti-HBs levels. Therefore, the present findings do not establish systemic inflammation as a determinant of longitudinal antibody persistence. Further longitudinal studies are required to determine whether systemic inflammatory markers have clinical utility in post-vaccination immunity monitoring.

title: Family cluster screening may help identify hepatitis D virus infections among individuals from highly endemic regions.
abstract: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection is the most severe form of chronic viral hepatitis and may remain substantially underdiagnosed, particularly among individuals originating from highly endemic regions. We report a Romanian family cluster identified through cascade screening following the diagnosis of an index case living in Spain. Six household contacts and first-degree relatives underwent hepatitis B virus (HBV) and HDV screening, identifying three additional cases of chronic HDV infection. Notably, all affected individuals had advanced liver disease at diagnosis, and two subsequently required liver transplantation. Two patients reported having been aware of their HBV diagnosis but were no longer engaged to healthcare follow-up and had not undergone HDV screening. This family cluster highlights the potential value of cascade screening of household contacts and first-degree relatives for identifying HDV infection, particularly among families originating from HDV-endemic regions. It also illustrates the clinical consequences of delayed diagnosis, including presentation with advanced liver disease and limited therapeutic opportunities. Family cluster case-finding could therefore represent a useful complementary strategy to systematic HDV screening in at-risk populations.

analysis.summary_en: This study highlights the importance of family cluster screening in identifying hepatitis D virus (HDV) infections among individuals from highly endemic regions. The research reports a Romanian family cluster where cascade screening following the diagnosis of an index case in Spain revealed three additional chronic HDV infections. Notably, two of the affected individuals had advanced liver disease and required liver transplantation. The findings suggest that cascade screening of household contacts and first-degree relatives may be a valuable strategy for detecting HDV infections, especially in populations at risk. The study also emphasizes the clinical consequences of delayed diagnosis, such as advanced liver disease and limited treatment options. However, the study is limited to a single family cluster, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the small sample size and the focus on a specific case.

title: Knowledge, attitudes and practices regarding prevention of hepatitis B virus mother-to-child transmission among health professionals in a semi-rural health district of Cameroon: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health problem in Cameroon, a country of high endemicity where mother-to-child transmission accounts for a substantial proportion of chronic infections, with more than 90% of infections acquired at birth progressing to chronicity compared with less than 5% among adults. Prevention of HBV mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) depends directly on the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of health workers providing maternity and immunization services, which remain poorly documented in semi-urban and rural health districts of Cameroon. This study aimed to assess these three dimensions among health professionals in the Obala Health District and to identify the factors associated with each. Methods An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted from April to June 2026 among health workers providing antenatal, maternity, and immunization services across the 33 health facilities of the Obala Health District, Centre Region, Cameroon. All 145 eligible staff were approached exhaustively; data were collected using a structured, pre-tested questionnaire under strict conditions of anonymity and confidentiality, and analyzed using IBM SPSS version 27.0. Scores were expressed as a percentage of the theoretical maximum and dichotomized at the 85% threshold (good/appropriate/adequate versus the remaining categories combined) for multivariable analysis. Multivariable binary logistic regression identified factors associated with good knowledge, appropriate attitudes, and adequate practices at p

analysis.study_design_and_population: This study aimed to assess these three dimensions among health professionals in the Obala Health District and to identify the factors associated with each.
analysis.methods: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted from April to June 2026 among health workers providing antenatal, maternity, and immunization services across the 33 health facilities of the Obala Health District, Centre Region, Cameroon. All 145 eligible staff were approached exhaustively; data were collected using a structured, pre-tested questionnaire under strict conditions of anonymity and confidentiality, and analyzed using IBM SPSS version 27.0.
analysis.main_results: Scores were expressed as a percentage of the theoretical maximum and dichotomized at the 85% threshold (good/appropriate/adequate versus the remaining categories combined) for multivariable analysis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Prevention of HBV mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) depends directly on the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of health workers providing maternity and immunization services, which remain poorly documented in semi-urban and rural health districts of Cameroon.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted interventions to improve health professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding PMTCT in semi-rural health districts of Cameroon.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to an abstract-only analysis, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of detailed results and statistical analyses.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of health professionals in the Obala Health District of Cameroon regarding the prevention of hepatitis B virus (HBV) mother-to-child transmission. The study highlights the critical role of health workers in PMTCT and identifies the need for improved documentation of these practices in semi-urban and rural health districts. The findings suggest that targeted interventions could enhance PMTCT efforts, but the study's evidence strength is moderate due to its abstract-only nature. The research underscores the importance of understanding health professionals' behaviors in combating HBV transmission, particularly in high-endemicity regions.

source_body_en: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health problem in Cameroon, a country of high endemicity where mother-to-child transmission accounts for a substantial proportion of chronic infections, with more than 90% of infections acquired at birth progressing to chronicity compared with less than 5% among adults. Prevention of HBV mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) depends directly on the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of health workers providing maternity and immunization services, which remain poorly documented in semi-urban and rural health districts of Cameroon. This study aimed to assess these three dimensions among health professionals in the Obala Health District and to identify the factors associated with each. Methods An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted from April to June 2026 among health workers providing antenatal, maternity, and immunization services across the 33 health facilities of the Obala Health District, Centre Region, Cameroon. All 145 eligible staff were approached exhaustively; data were collected using a structured, pre-tested questionnaire under strict conditions of anonymity and confidentiality, and analyzed using IBM SPSS version 27.0. Scores were expressed as a percentage of the theoretical maximum and dichotomized at the 85% threshold (good/appropriate/adequate versus the remaining categories combined) for multivariable analysis. title: Completion of Hepatitis B Vaccination Schedule Among Healthcare Workers in Four Counties in Kenya: A Mixed-Methods Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Healthcare workers (HCWs) are at an increased risk of hepatitis B virus infection through occupational exposure, yet completion of the recommended hepatitis B vaccination schedule remains suboptimal in Kenya. We assessed vaccination completion, associated factors, motivators, and barriers among HCWs. Methods: We conducted a mixed-methods study combining a cross-sectional survey of 1614 HCWs in 178 health facilities across Kakamega, Nakuru, Mombasa, and Siaya counties with nine focus group discussions. The survey was conducted in August–September 2023 and the focus groups during June 2024–January 2025. Mixed-effects logistic regression with a random intercept for health facility was used to identify factors associated with completion of three vaccine doses, and qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Results: Among 1583 HCWs with a known vaccination status, 700 (44.2%; 95% CI: 41.8–46.7) reported completing three doses, 410 (25.9%) had received one or two doses, and 473 (29.9%) had never been vaccinated. The main motivator was self-protection (71.7%). Common barriers were vaccine unavailability (57.5%), lack of knowledge (28.8%), the vaccine not being offered on site (28.2%), and cost (17.4%). Completion was more likely among male HCWs, those working in urban areas facilities, and those with 6–10 or 11–20 years of healthcare work experience, and less likely among support staff, administrative staff, clinicians and allied health professionals than among nurses/midwives. Conclusions: Fewer than half of HCWs reported completing the three-dose hepatitis B vaccination schedule. Improving vaccine availability, reducing out-of-pocket costs, strengthening dose-reminder systems, and addressing knowledge gaps may improve completion among HCWs in the study counties.

abstract_zh: 背景/目标:医疗工作者(HCWs)因职业暴露而面临更高的乙型肝炎病毒感染风险,但在肯尼亚完成推荐的乙型肝炎疫苗接种接种计划仍不理想。我们评估了医疗工作者完成三剂疫苗接种接种计划的情况、相关因素、动机和障碍。方法:我们开展了一项混合方法研究,结合了在肯尼亚卡卡梅加、纳库鲁、蒙巴萨和西亚县178家医疗机构中对1614名医疗工作者的横断面调查,以及九次焦点小组讨论。调查于2023年8月至9月进行,焦点小组讨论于2024年6月至2025年1月进行。采用带有医疗机构随机截距的混合效应逻辑回归模型,以确定完成三剂疫苗接种接种计划的相关因素,并对定性数据进行了主题分析。结果:在1583名已知疫苗接种状态的医疗工作者中,700人(44.2%;95% CI:41.8–46.7)报告已完成三剂接种,410人(25.9%)接种了一剂或两剂,473人(29.9%)从未接种过疫苗。主要动机是自我保护(71.7%)。常见的障碍包括疫苗不可用(57.5%)、缺乏知识(28.8%)、疫苗未在机构内提供(28.2%)以及费用(17.4%)。完成接种的比例在男性医疗工作者、在城市地区工作的医疗工作者以及有6–10年或11–20年医疗工作经验的医疗工作者中更高,而在支持人员、行政人员、临床医生和相关医疗专业人员中较低,相较于护士/助产士。结论:在研究的四个县中,不到一半的医疗工作者报告完成了三剂乙型肝炎疫苗接种接种计划。提高疫苗的可获得性、降低自费费用、加强接种提醒系统以及解决知识差距可能有助于提高这些县医疗工作者的接种完成率。

title: Comparative Clinical, Demographic, and Cardiometabolic Profile of Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Patients in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: A Cross- Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Background and Objectives Pakistan is disproportionately affected by HBV and HCV, which continue to be important causes of chronic liver disease. Although there is little evidence in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, worldwide data indicates that infected individuals have different cardiometabolic and demographic characteristics. This study identified independent predictors of hepatitis type by comparing the demographic, cardiometabolic, and clinical characteristics of individuals with HBV and HCV. Methodology This comparative cross-sectional study included 549 laboratory-confirmed patients (249 HBV-positive, 300 HCV-positive) recruited from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Demographic, anthropometric, cardiometabolic, vaccination, and symptom data were extracted from clinical records; hypertension was defined using the 2017 ACC/AHA threshold, and presenting symptoms were grouped into seven clinical domains. Normality was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test; as continuous variables were non-normally distributed, between-group comparisons used the Mann-Whitney U test, while categorical variables were compared using the Pearson Chi-square test with Cramér's V as effect size. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with hepatitis type, with model fit assessed via the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test and Nagelkerke R2. Results HBV patients were significantly older than HCV patients (41.03±10.61 vs. 36.64±10.35 years, p Conclusion HBV and HCV patients exhibit distinct cardiometabolic risk profiles despite comparable symptom presentation. Hypertension emerged as the strongest independent correlate of hepatitis type, underscoring the value of adjusted analysis in hepatitis comorbidity research.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Background and Objectives Pakistan is disproportionately affected by HBV and HCV, which continue to be important causes of chronic liver disease. Although there is little evidence in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, worldwide data indicates that infected individuals have different cardiometabolic and demographic characteristics. This study identified independent predictors of hepatitis type by comparing the demographic, cardiometabolic, and clinical characteristics of individuals with HBV and HCV. Methodology This comparative cross-sectional study included 549 laboratory-confirmed patients (249 HBV-positive, 300 HCV-positive) recruited from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Demographic, anthropometric, cardiometabolic, vaccination, and symptom data were extracted from clinical records; hypertension was defined using the 2017 ACC/AHA threshold, and presenting symptoms were grouped into seven clinical domains. Normality was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test; as continuous variables were non-normally distributed, between-group comparisons used the Mann-Whitney U test, while categorical variables were compared using the Pearson Chi-square test with Cramér's V as effect size. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to identify factors independently associated with hepatitis type, with model fit assessed via the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test and Nagelkerke R2. Results HBV patients were significantly older than HCV patients (41.03±10.61 vs. 36.64±10.35 years, p Conclusion HBV and HCV patients exhibit distinct cardiometabolic risk profiles despite comparable symptom presentation. Hypertension emerged as the strongest independent correlate of hepatitis type, underscoring the value of adjusted analysis in hepatitis comorbidity research.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景与目的 巴基斯坦的乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)和丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)感染情况异常严重,仍然是慢性肝病的重要病因。尽管在开伯尔-普什图省(Khyber Pakhtunkhwa)缺乏相关证据,但全球数据显示,感染个体在心血管代谢和人口统计学特征上存在差异。本研究通过比较HBV和HCV感染个体的人口统计学、心血管代谢和临床特征,以确定肝炎类型的独立预测因素。方法 这项比较性横断面研究纳入了549名实验室确诊的患者(249名HBV阳性,300名HCV阳性),来自巴基斯坦开伯尔-普什图省。人口统计学、人体测量学、心血管代谢、疫苗接种以及症状数据均从临床记录中提取;高血压采用2017年ACC/AHA标准定义,临床症状被分为七个临床领域。通过Shapiro-Wilk检验评估数据的正态性;对于非正态分布的连续变量,采用Mann-Whitney U检验进行组间比较,而分类变量则采用Pearson卡方检验,并以Cramér's V作为效应量。通过多变量二元逻辑回归分析确定与肝炎类型独立相关的因素,模型拟合度通过Hosmer-Lemeshow拟合优度检验和Nagelkerke R2进行评估。结果 HBV患者的年龄显著高于HCV患者(41.03±10.61岁 vs. 36.64±10.35岁,p < 0.001)。高血压是肝炎类型最强的独立相关因素。结论 尽管HBV和HCV患者的症状表现相似,但两者在心血管代谢风险特征上存在显著差异,这表明在管理这些感染时需要采取针对性的策略。

title: Mapping Hepatitis B Virus Research and Genomic Diversity in Latin America and the Caribbean
abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health challenge in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). Mapping scientific production and viral genomic diversity is essential to identify consolidated research fields, as well as areas of opportunity to improve and expand research across the region. Methods: An integrated analysis combining bibliometrics, text-mining, and phylogenetics was performed on HBV literature indexed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (1970–2025), alongside 9528 GenBank sequences (including full-length genomes, individual genes, and partial diagnostic fragments). Results: A total of 4083 publications were identified, of which 72.1% (2942/4083) were from Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina. Most were original articles (75.8%; 2749/3628) involving human cohorts (95.8%; 2471/2580), where primary research fields centered on serological profiling, co-infections, vaccination, genotype characterization, and blood safety, whereas hepatocellular carcinoma, antiviral therapy, and metabolic comorbidities were the least frequently studied areas. In vitro (10.1%; 260/2580) and animal models (6.9%; 177/2580) accounted for a minor fraction of the literature. Eight circulating HBV genotypes (A–H) were detected, dominated by A (43.4%; 4138/9528), F (29.3%; 2787/9528), and D (19.8%; 1885/9528), while genotype H was largely confined to Mexico (3.2%; 306/9528). Marked geographic clustering was observed (p < 0.001), reflecting both autochthonous American and immigrant lineages. Conclusions: Epidemiological studies represent the most consolidated domain in LAC, yet research remains concentrated in a few countries with persistent experimental and clinical gaps. Fostering cross-border collaboration and investing in underexplored translational areas will be decisive in achieving regional hepatitis B elimination.

Methods: An integrated analysis combining bibliometrics, text-mining, and phylogenetics was performed on HBV literature indexed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (1970–2025), alongside 9528 GenBank sequences (including full-length genomes, individual genes, and partial diagnostic fragments). Results: A total of 4083 publications were identified, of which 72.1% (2942/4083) were from Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina. Most were original articles (75.8%; 2749/3628) involving human cohorts (95.8%; 2471/2580), where primary research fields centered on serological profiling, co-infections, vaccination, genotype characterization, and blood safety, whereas hepatocellular carcinoma, antiviral therapy, and metabolic comorbidities were the least frequently studied areas. In vitro (10.1%; 260/2580) and animal models (6.9%; 177/2580) accounted for a minor fraction of the literature. Eight circulating HBV genotypes (A–H) were detected, dominated by A (43.4%; 4138/9528), F (29.3%; 2787/9528), and D (19.8%; 1885/9528), while genotype H was largely confined to Mexico (3.2%; 306/9528). Marked geographic clustering was observed (p < 0.001), reflecting both autochthonous American and immigrant lineages. Conclusions: Epidemiological studies represent the most consolidated domain in LAC, yet research remains concentrated in a few countries with persistent experimental and clinical gaps. Fostering cross-border collaboration and investing in underexplored translational areas will be decisive in achieving regional hepatitis B elimination.

abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染仍然是拉丁美洲和加勒比地区(LAC)的主要公共卫生挑战。绘制科学生产图谱和病毒基因组多样性对于识别已确立的研究领域以及改善和扩展该地区研究的机会至关重要。方法:对PubMed、Scopus和Web of Science(1970–2025)中索引的HBV文献以及9528条GenBank序列(包括完整的乙型肝炎病毒基因组、单个基因和部分诊断片段)进行了整合分析,结合了文献计量学、文本挖掘和系统发育分析。结果:共识别出4083篇文献,其中72.1%(2942/4083)来自巴西、墨西哥和阿根廷。大多数为原始研究文章(75.8%;2749/3628),涉及人类乙型肝炎病毒(95.8%;2471/2580),主要研究领域集中在血清学特征分析、共感染、慢性乙型肝炎、基因型特征分析和血液安全方面,而肝细胞癌、慢性乙型肝炎治疗和代谢共病则是研究较少的领域。体外研究(10.1%;260/2580)和动物模型(6.9%;177/2580)仅占文献的一小部分。检测到8种流行的HBV基因型(A–H),其中A型(43.4%;4138/9528)、F型(29.3%;2787/9528)和D型(19.8%;1885/9528)占主导地位,而H型基因型主要局限于墨西哥(3.2%;306/9528)。观察到显著的地理聚集性(p < 0.001),反映了本地的美洲和移民的病毒谱系。结论:流行病学研究是LAC中最稳固的研究领域,但研究仍集中在少数国家,存在持续的实验和临床研究空白。促进跨境合作并投资于未被充分探索的转化研究领域,将是实现该地区乙肝消除的关键。

title: Global prevalence of hepatitis B among displaced populations (internally-displaced persons, refugees, and asylum seekers): a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Displaced persons, including internally displaced persons (IDPs), refugees and asylum seekers, are vulnerable to several diseases, including hepatitis B. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the global prevalence of hepatitis B among displaced persons and their subgroups. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guideline was followed in this review. Relevant published studies were searched from eight academic databases from 2016 to 2026, with additional citation searching. After screening, relevant data were extracted from each included study and assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist. Using Stata 15.0, the random-effects model of DerSimonian and Laird, with the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation, was used to pool the estimates. Heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 and Cochran’s Q test, and the sources were traced using subgroup and meta-regression analyses. The leave-out-one sensitivity analysis was used to test study’s robustness. Publication bias was assessed using Egger regression test and funnel plot visualisation. The search strategy identified 4,673 records, and 117 were included. The pooled prevalence of hepatitis B was 3.86% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.45–4.29%). The prevalence was higher among males, 5.98% (CI: 4.61–7.50%), compared to females, 3.82% (CI: 2.96–4.78%), while children and adolescents recorded lower rates at 1.56% (CI: 1.01–2.20%). The prevalence was highest among those from Eastern Asia, 11.62% (CI: 7.61–16.32%), South-eastern Asia, 7.18% (CI: 5.70–8.80%), and Sub-Saharan Africa, 6.62% (CI: 5.44–7.90%). Subgroup analysis indicated significantly higher ( p ≤ 0.05) pooled prevalence among IDPs, 9.99% (CI: 6.82–13.67%), those hosted in Africa, 7.74% (CI: 5.02–10.97%), and in displacement camps, 7.19% (CI: 5.47–9.11%). Considerable heterogeneity remained after subgroup analyses and multivariate meta-regression linked the heterogeneity to displacement status, male percentage, temporal design and study settings. Sensitivity analysis demonstrated the robustness of findings, while Egger’s regression test and funnel plot asymmetry indicated small-study effect. In conclusion, displaced persons have a high burden of hepatitis B compared to the general population, with being male, an IDP, of Eastern Asian origin, residing in displacement camps, and being from Africa associated with higher risk. Hence, government and non-governmental organisations are encouraged to prioritise them in their hepatitis B control efforts.

title_zh: 全球乙型肝炎在流离失所人群中的患病率(包括内部流离失所者、难民和寻求庇护者):一项系统综述和荟萃分析
source_body_en: Displaced persons, including internally displaced persons (IDPs), refugees and asylum seekers, are vulnerable to several diseases, including hepatitis B. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the global prevalence of hepatitis B among displaced persons and their subgroups. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guideline was followed in this review. Relevant published studies were searched from eight academic databases from 2016 to 2026, with additional citation searching. After screening, relevant data were extracted from each included study and assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist. Using Stata 15.0, the random-effects model of DerSimonian and Laird, with the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation, was used to pool the estimates. Heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 and Cochran’s Q test, and the sources were traced using subgroup and meta-regression analyses. The leave-out-one sensitivity analysis was used to test study’s robustness. Publication bias was assessed using Egger regression test and funnel plot visualisation. The search strategy identified 4,673 records, and 117 were included. The pooled prevalence of hepatitis B was 3.86% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.45–4.29%). The prevalence was higher among males, 5.98% (CI: 4.61–7.50%), compared to females, 3.82% (CI: 2.96–4.78%), while children and adolescents recorded lower rates at 1.56% (CI: 1.01–2.20%). The prevalence was highest among those from Eastern Asia, 11.62% (CI: 7.61–16.32%), South-eastern Asia, 7.18% (CI: 5.70–8.80%), and Sub-Saharan Africa, 6.62% (CI: 5.44–7.90%). Subgroup analysis indicated significantly higher ( p ≤ 0.05) pooled prevalence among IDPs, 9.99% (CI: 6.82–13.67%), those hosted in Africa, 7.74% (CI: 5.02–10.97%), and in displacement camps, 7.19% (CI: 5.47–9.11%). Considerable heterogeneity remained after subgroup analyses and multivariate meta-regression linked the heterogeneity to displacement status, male percentage, temporal design and study settings. Sensitivity analysis demonstrated the robustness of findings, while Egger’s regression test and funnel plot asymmetry indicated small-study effect. In conclusion, displaced persons have a high burden of hepatitis B compared to the general population, with being male, an IDP, of Eastern Asian origin, residing in displacement camps, and being from Africa associated with higher risk. Hence, government and non-governmental organisations are encouraged to prioritise them in their hepatitis B control efforts.

title: The prevalence of and factors associated with hepatitis B and hepatitis C among men who have sex with men in Kigali, Rwanda
abstract: Rwanda has scaled up its viral hepatitis B (HBV) and C (HCV) prevention and treatment programs over the last decade. However, data to guide HBV and HCV programming for men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women (TGW) are limited. This analysis characterizes the epidemiology of HBV and HCV among MSM and TGW in Kigali, Rwanda. We leveraged stored plasma samples of 729 MSM/TGW recruited in Kigali using respondent-driven sampling (RDS) conducted between March and August 2018. Rapid diagnostic tests were used to screen for HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) and HCV antibodies (HCVAb). Viral load (VL) testing for HBV and HCV was performed for all positive samples. Approximate Bayesian logistic regression models using penalized likelihood estimation via data augmentation were used to assess factors associated with HBsAg and HCVAb positivity; adjusted odds ratios (aOR) and 95% profile-likelihood limits (PLL) from these models are reported. The mean age was 25 years (IQR: 22–31; range:18–68); 14.4% ( n = 106) of participants were TGW. Prevalence of HBsAg was 3.4% (25/729; RDS adjusted: 2.7%,95%CI: 1.2% – 4.2%). Most, 92.0%(23/25) had detectable HBV DNA, the median HBV DNA was 3.0 (IQR:1.9–3.7) log 10 IU/ml. Age (aOR:1.04; 95%PLL:1.00-1.09), having sexual partners who ever injected drugs (aOR:3.13; 95%PLL:1.51–6.53), and reporting STI symptoms in the year preceding study entry (aOR:2.11; 95% PLL:1.03–4.34) were associated with HBsAg positivity. HCVAb was detected in 1.6% (12/729; RDS adjusted: 1.7% (95%CI: 0.7% − 2.7%), including 33.3% (4/12) with detectable HCV RNA. Age was the only factor significantly associated with HCVAb positivity (aOR:1.06; 95%PLL:1.01–1.12). Ongoing screening for viral hepatitis among MSM and TGW in Rwanda is needed and can strengthen viral hepatitis prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) screening programs. The prevalence of HBV and HCV was highest among MSM/TGW aged 35 and older(HBsAg 7.6%; HCVAb 3.8%), a group in which we previously found higher prevalence of HIV and other STIs. Interventions tailored to the needs of older MSM/TGW are needed. Finally, the high burden of HBV among individuals whose partners inject drugs suggests that the networks of MSM/TGW who inject drugs overlap with the networks of those who do not inject drugs. For optimal public health impact, MSM/TGW programming should consider addressing both injection drug use and sex-related acquisition and transmission risks.
