title: Sexual dysfunction, depressive symptoms, and perceived impact of HBV infectivity among noncirrhotic patients with chronic hepatitis B: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global public health burden, yet sexual health is rarely addressed in routine care. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of sexual dysfunction (SD) and examine demographic, clinical, and psychological factors associated with sexual function among noncirrhotic patients with CHB. We also explored the association between sexual function and the perceived negative impact of HBV infectivity on sexual life. Methods This cross-sectional study was conducted from December 2023 to July 2024, enrolling 657 patients with CHB and 121 non-HBV controls. Patients with CHB were classified by treatment status as receiving pegylated interferon α-2b ( n = 391), receiving nucleos(t)ide analogues ( n = 203), or not receiving antiviral therapy ( n = 63). Sexual function was assessed using the IIEF-5, EHS, and PEDT in men and the FSFI in women. Psychological status was assessed with the PHQ-9 and GAD-7, and the perceived negative impact of HBV infectivity on sexual life was assessed using a single exploratory yes/no item. Hierarchical multiple linear regression was used to identify factors associated with sexual function scores. Results The prevalence of SD was significantly higher in all CHB subgroups than in Non-HBV group, with the highest prevalence observed in the IFN-CHB group, both in men (70.9%) and women (70.8%). In multivariable models, older age, IFN-CHB status, and higher PHQ-9 scores were associated with lower sexual function scores in both sexes. Of the variables examined, IFN-CHB status showed the strongest negative association in men ( β = −0.267, p < 0.001), whereas PHQ-9 score showed the strongest negative association in women ( β = −0.312, p = 0.006). A perceived negative impact of HBV infectivity on sexual life was reported by 21.6% of men and 24.7% of women with CHB. Men reporting this perception had lower IIEF-5 scores ( p < 0.001), and women reporting it had lower FSFI scores ( p = 0.020). Conclusion Sexual dysfunction was common among sexually active patients with CHB, and poorer sexual function was associated with IFN-CHB status, depressive symptoms, and the perceived negative impact of HBV infectivity on sexual life. Sexual health assessment and mental health support may therefore have value in comprehensive CHB care.

abstract_zh: 背景 慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)仍是全球主要公共卫生负担,但性健康在常规治疗中很少被关注。本研究旨在评估CHB患者中性功能障碍(SD)的患病率,并探讨与性功能相关的流行病学、临床和心理因素。我们还研究了性功能与HBV传染性对性生活负面影响的感知之间的关联。方法 本项横断面研究于2023年12月至2024年7月进行,纳入了657名CHB患者和121名非HBV对照者。根据治疗状态,CHB患者被分为三组:接受聚乙二醇干扰素α-2b治疗(n=391)、接受核苷(酸)类似物治疗(n=203)或未接受抗病毒药物治疗(n=63)。男性性功能通过IIEF-5、EHS和PEDT评估,女性则通过FSFI评估。心理状态通过PHQ-9和GAD-7评估,HBV传染性对性生活的负面影响则通过一个探索性单选是/否问题进行评估。采用分层多元线性回归分析以确定与性功能评分相关的因素。结果 所有CHB亚组中性功能障碍的患病率均显著高于非HBV组,其中IFN-CHB组的患病率最高,男性为70.9%,女性为70.8%。在多变量模型中,年龄较大、IFN-CHB状态以及较高的PHQ-9评分均与两性较低的性功能评分相关。在所研究的变量中,IFN-CHB状态在男性中显示出最强的负相关(β=-0.267,p<0.001),而PHQ-9评分在女性中显示出最强的负相关(β=-0.312,p=0.006)。在CHB患者中,有21.6%的男性和24.7%的女性报告了HBV传染性对性生活产生负面影响的感知。报告该感知的男性IIEF-5评分较低(p<0.001),报告该感知的女性FSFI评分较低(p=0.020)。结论 在性活跃的CHB患者中,性功能障碍较为常见,较差的性功能与IFN-CHB状态、抑郁症状以及HBV传染性对性生活的负面影响感知相关。因此,在全面的CHB治疗中,评估性健康和提供心理健康支持可能具有重要价值。

title: Fatal Hepatitis B Virus Reactivation Following Immunosuppressive Therapy in a Patient with an Atypical Hepatitis B Virus Serological Profile: A Case Report
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation is a well-recognized complication in patients with lymphoma receiving immunosuppressive therapy, particularly rituximab-containing regimens. We describe a 58-year-old man with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and an atypical baseline HBV serological profile: hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) positivity (102.00 U/L), antibody to hepatitis B core antigen negativity, a low-level hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) result (0.35 COI, reported as negative by the local laboratory), and undetectable HBV DNA. Thirteen days after initiation of the fourth cycle of modified R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, pirarubicin, vinorelbine and dexamethasone) chemoimmunotherapy, the anti-HBs titer had decreased to 1.31 S/CO, the HBsAg level to 0.02 S/CO, and HBV DNA was not reassessed until reactivation. Approximately 16 weeks after treatment completion, the patient developed fatigue, anorexia, and jaundice. HBsAg increased from 28.66 S/CO to 8048.30 IU/mL, hepatitis B e antigen became positive, and HBV DNA increased to 1.94 × 109 IU/mL. Despite treatment with tenofovir alafenamide fumarate and plasma exchange, the patient died of refractory liver failure and hepatic encephalopathy. These findings suggest that atypical serological profiles may not reliably indicate a low risk of severe HBV reactivation during intensive immunosuppressive therapy. analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 58-year-old man with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and an atypical HBV serological profile who experienced fatal HBV reactivation following immunosuppressive therapy. The patient had anti-HBs positivity, HBsAg low-level positivity, and undetectable HBV DNA at baseline. After treatment with modified R-CHOP, his anti-HBs titer decreased, HBsAg increased significantly, and HBV DNA levels rose to 1.94 × 109 IU/mL. Despite treatment with tenofovir alafenamide fumarate and plasma exchange, the patient died of refractory liver failure and hepatic encephalopathy. The study underscores the importance of comprehensive pretreatment risk assessment and ongoing monitoring of HBV markers during and after immunosuppressive therapy. The evidence is based on a single case report, which limits its generalizability and strength.

title: Prevalence of Hepatitis B Virus Infection among Barbers and Butchers
abstract: Background: Barbers and butchers handle sharp instruments that are frequently contaminated with blood, placing them at increased occupational risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. This study estimated the prevalence of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) among barbers and butchers in Salah Al-Din Governorate, Iraq, compared with unexposed controls, and described the demographic and occupational characteristics of HBsAg-positive workers. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted from January to June 2025 and enrolled 900 participants aged 20–70 years: 300 barbers, 300 butchers, and 300 healthy male controls. Serum HBsAg was detected by ELISA; reactive samples were retested for confirmation. Groups were compared using the chi-square or Fisher's exact test, P < 0.05 was considered significant. Results: HBsAg was detected in barbers (11.3%) and butchers (9.3%) but in none of the controls (0%), a difference that was highly significant. Prevalence did not differ significantly between barbers and butchers .Among barbers, positivity was associated with age, whereas no age association was found among butchers. About three-fifths of positive workers in both groups were asymptomatic. Work-related cuts were reported by 52.9% of positive barbers (P < 0.001). Conclusion: Barbers and butchers carry a burden of HBV infection six to seven times that of the general population, attributable to frequent occupational cuts and to instrument-cleaning practices that do not inactivate the virus; most infections are clinically silent. These occupational groups should be prioritized for HBV vaccination, periodic serological screening.
journal: International Journal of Biological and Pharmaceutical Sciences Archive

title: Casual analysis between screening adherence and hepatocellular carcinoma staging in hepatitis B patients: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Current clinical guidelines recommend that chronic hepatitis B patients undergo abdominal ultrasound and alpha-fetoprotein testing every six months. However, most of these patients exhibit insufficient screening adherence. This study aimed to determine whether screening adherence directly affects the tumor stage in patients with chronic hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma. This single-center, observational, retrospective cohort study enrolled 150 patients with chronic hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma who were treated at the Department of Infectious Diseases, Third Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, from 2008 to 2023. Stabilized inverse probability weighting was used to balance confounding factors. Screening adherence was defined as the completion rate of regular semiannual screenings. It was calculated as (6 × number of screenings) ÷ follow-up duration in months. The primary outcome measures were advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (China Liver Cancer Staging IIb–IV) and maximum tumor diameter. Multivariate regression models were constructed to assess causal associations. Confounding factors included age, gender, cirrhosis, nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy, alcohol consumption, hepatitis B e antigen, hepatitis B virus DNA, and alpha-fetoprotein. After inverse probability weighting, the standardized mean differences for all confounding factors were less than 0.1. Weighted logistic regression revealed that screening adherence was an independent protective factor against advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (OR, 0.209; 95% CI, 0.061–0.716; p = 0.013). Weighted multiple linear regression demonstrated a significant inverse correlation between screening adherence and maximum tumor diameter (coefficient, −1.851; 95% CI, −3.137 to −0.565; p = 0.005). Insufficient adherence to hepatocellular carcinoma screening among chronic hepatitis B patients results in missed optimal diagnostic windows. This significantly increases the risk of advanced cancer. All interested parties should collaborate to develop feasible strategies for improving patient adherence.

title: Predictors of Antibody Response to Hepatitis B Vaccination in Hemodialysis Patients.
abstract: End-stage renal disease (ESRD) patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis are at high risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and demonstrate inadequate immune response to vaccination. The objective of the study was to assess the antibody response (anti-HBs levels) of hepatitis B vaccinated maintenance hemodialysis patients. This cross-sectional observational analytical study was conducted at Marine City Medical College Hospital, Chittagong, Bangladesh for 34 months of period among 50 patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis for more than 4 months. Demographic and clinical data were collected and post-vaccination anti-HBs titers were measured. Patients were classified as high responders (anti-HBs ≥100 mIU/ml), poor responders (anti-HBs ≥10 to 50 years, presence of diabetes mellitus and lower serum albumin were significantly associated with poor or non response (p<0.05). Development of protective antibody levels after hepatitis B vaccination in maintenance hemodialysis patients was inadequate. Older age, diabetes and low serum albumin were important predictors of poor response. Strategies such as booster dosing and revaccination may improve seroconversion rates in this population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hemodialysis patients are at high risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and show inadequate immune response to vaccination. The study aimed to assess predictors of antibody response to hepatitis B vaccination in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional observational analytical study was conducted at Marine City Medical College Hospital, Chittagong, Bangladesh over 34 months among 50 patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis for more than 4 months.
analysis.methods: Demographic and clinical data were collected, and post-vaccination anti-HBs titers were measured to classify patients as high responders or poor responders.
analysis.main_results: Older age, presence of diabetes mellitus, and lower serum albumin were significantly associated with poor or non-response to hepatitis B vaccination (p<0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight that certain clinical factors are important predictors of inadequate antibody response to hepatitis B vaccination in hemodialysis patients.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform strategies for improving seroconversion rates in hemodialysis patients through targeted interventions such as booster dosing and revaccination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and small sample size, but the evidence is strong given the clear association between clinical factors and poor response.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated predictors of antibody response to hepatitis B vaccination in hemodialysis patients. It found that older age, diabetes mellitus, and lower serum albumin levels were significantly associated with poor or non-response. These findings suggest that targeted strategies such as booster dosing and revaccination may improve seroconversion rates in this vulnerable population. The study was conducted as a cross-sectional observational analytical study at a single hospital in Bangladesh over 34 months, involving 50 patients. While the study provides important insights, its small sample size and observational design limit the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the clear statistical associations reported.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面观察性分析研究在孟加拉国吉大港的海洋城医学院医院进行,持续时间为34个月,研究对象为接受维持性血液透析超过4个月的50名患者。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,某些临床因素是维持性血液透析患者对乙型肝炎疫苗接种抗体反应不足的重要预测因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为通过针对性干预措施(如加强剂量接种和重新接种)提高维持性血液透析患者的血清转换率提供依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到观察性设计和小样本量的限制,但鉴于临床因素与不良反应之间的明确关联,其证据是强有力的。

title: In vitro and in vivo studies of medicinal plants against hepatitis B and hepatitis C infections: A narrative review
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections remain major global health problems. This review summarizes current evidence on medicinal plants with reported antiviral activity against HBV and HCV, focusing on experimental models and underlying molecular mechanisms. A narrative review approach was used to identify and present relevant studies from PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar using keywords related to hepatitis viruses and medicinal plants. Relevant studies were selected based on their relevance to the topic, particularly those reporting antiviral activity in in vitro and in vivo models. The findings were synthesized narratively by organizing the evidence according to plant species, extract types, viral targets, and mechanisms of antiviral action. Medicinal plants contained diverse bioactive compounds with antiviral potential, including flavonoids, alkaloids, chalcones, polysaccharides, and polyphenols. Evidence from in vitro and in vivo studies indicates that these compounds may inhibit viral attachment and entry, suppress polymerase activity, reduce hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) secretion, interfere with capsid assembly, and inhibit HCV non-structural proteins. Notable compounds such as epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), silibinin, quercetin derivatives, and solanopubamine demonstrated reductions in viral nucleic acid levels and improvements in liver-related outcomes in experimental models. Medicinal plants are promising antiviral sources against HBV and HCV due to their multi-target bioactive compounds. However, variability in extracts and limited clinical evidence require further standardized and clinical studies to confirm their therapeutic use.

abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)和丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)感染仍然是全球主要的健康问题。本综述总结了当前关于具有抗病毒药物活性的药用植物对HBV和HCV作用的证据,重点探讨了实验模型和潜在的分子机制。采用叙述性综述的方法,通过与肝炎病毒和药用植物相关的关键词,在PubMed、Scopus、ScienceDirect和Google Scholar中识别并呈现相关研究。相关研究的选择基于其与主题的相关性,特别是那些在体外和体内模型中报告抗病毒药物活性的研究。通过按植物种类、提取物类型、病毒靶点以及抗病毒药物作用机制来组织证据,对研究结果进行了叙述性综合。药用植物含有多种具有抗病毒药物潜力的生物活性化合物,包括黄酮类、生物碱、查尔酮、多糖和多酚。体外和体内研究的证据表明,这些化合物可能抑制病毒附着和进入,抑制聚合酶活性,减少乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)和乙型肝炎e抗原(HBeAg)的分泌,干扰衣壳组装,并抑制HCV非结构蛋白。一些显著的化合物,如表没食子儿茶素没食子酸酯(EGCG)、水飞蓟素、槲皮素衍生物和茄碱,已在实验模型中显示出降低病毒核酸水平并改善与肝脏相关结果的潜力。由于其多靶点生物活性化合物,药用植物在对抗HBV和HCV方面具有成为抗病毒药物来源的前景。然而,提取物的变异性以及临床证据有限,需要进一步标准化和临床研究以确认其治疗用途。

title: Biological interpretation of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis in determining interferon treatment duration
abstract: The recent identification of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as independent predictors of extended interferon therapy provides a valuable clinical framework, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these associations require further elucidation. In this opinion review, we interpret these factors not merely as statistical covariates but as pathological surrogates for the virus-host equilibrium. We propose that high baseline hepatitis B surface antigen may reflect a deeply entrenched intrahepatic viral reservoir and may create an antigen-rich environment that impairs effective antiviral immunity. Concurrently, cirrhosis may be better understood as a spectrum of architectural remodeling in which vascular changes and sinusoidal defenestration could limit immune surveillance and affect local therapeutic access. Consequently, treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks may be required, at least in part, to overcome these profound immunological and structural barriers. We advocate shifting future predictive modeling from binary clinical definitions to a granular integration of viral kinetics and histological morphology to refine precision medicine in chronic hepatitis B.

abstract_zh: 最近将基线乙型肝炎表面抗原和肝硬化确定为延长干扰素治疗的独立预测因子,提供了有价值的临床框架,但这些关联背后的生物学机制需要进一步阐明。在本意见综述中,我们不仅将这些因素解释为统计协变量,而且将其解释为病毒-宿主 平衡的病理替代物。我们认为,高基线乙型肝炎表面抗原可能反映了肝内根深蒂固的病毒 储存宿主,并可能创造一个富含抗原的环境,损害有效的 抗病毒药物 免疫力。同时,肝硬化可以更好地理解为一系列结构重塑,其中血管变化和肝窦开窗可能限制免疫 监测 并影响局部治疗途径。因此,可能需要(至少部分)超过 48 周的 治疗 持续时间来克服这些深刻的免疫学和结构障碍。我们主张将未来的预测模型从二元临床定义转变为病毒动力学和组织学形态的精细整合,以完善 慢性乙型肝炎 中的精准医学。

title: A Bayesian-Optimized Heterogeneous Stacking Framework with Comparative Explainable AI for Hepatitis B Diagnostic Support
abstract: Hepatitis B diagnosis requires the combined interpretation of viral-load markers, biochemical parameters, demographic information, and clinical symptoms. Developing a reliable machine-learning model for this purpose is challenging when the available clinical dataset is small and model development involves architecture selection, hyperparameter optimization, threshold selection, and explainability analysis. This study developed Bayes Stack-HBV, a Bayesian-optimized heterogeneous stacking framework intended to provide internally validated decision support for hepatitis B classification. The framework used nine predictors comprising two hundred sixteen patient records and combined heterogeneous base learners through an Elastic Net-regularized logistic meta-learner. Model architecture and hyperparameters were optimized using 40 Optuna trials within each outer-fold training set. Performance was evaluated using repeated nested cross-validation with three random seeds, five outer folds, and three inner folds. Preprocessing, SMOTE, model optimization, and decision-threshold selection were restricted to the training and inner-validation data. Bayes Stack-HBV was compared with Default Stack-HBV, Hist Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machine, Extra Trees, Logistic Regression, and K-Nearest Neighbors. Calibration, paired statistical comparisons, and multi-method explainability analyses were performed using held-out predictions. Across 15 held-out outer-fold evaluations, Bayes Stack-HBV achieved an accuracy of 0.9337 ± 0.0324, balanced accuracy of 0.9357 ± 0.0307, precision of 0.9659 ± 0.0383, sensitivity of 0.9114 ± 0.0670, specificity of 0.9600 ± 0.0471, F1-score of 0.9357 ± 0.0331, MCC of 0.8728 ± 0.0602, ROC-AUC of 0.9844 ± 0.0162, PR-AUC of 0.9892 ± 0.0103, and Brier score of 0.0428 ± 0.0188. Bayes Stack-HBV ranked first on seven of ten mean evaluation measures, indicating a strong specificity- and calibration-oriented performance profile. However, differences relative to the strongest ensemble comparators were not statistically significant after multiple-comparison correction. Explainability analysis identified HBVDNA and ALT Level as influential predictors, supported by expanded explanation-stability and feature-dependency analyses. Bayes Stack-HBV provides promising preliminary evidence as a threshold-aware and interpretable framework for HBV decision support. Its clinical utility and threshold transportability require confirmation through larger, independent, multicenter, and prospective validation studies.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a reliable machine-learning model for hepatitis B diagnosis by integrating diverse clinical data. The researchers created Bayes Stack-HBV, a Bayesian-optimized heterogeneous stacking framework, and evaluated its performance using repeated nested cross-validation. The model achieved high accuracy and specificity across multiple evaluation metrics, ranking first on seven of ten measures. However, the differences compared to other models were not statistically significant after multiple-comparison correction. The framework demonstrated strong calibration and explainability, with HBVDNA and ALT Level identified as influential predictors. Despite these results, the model's clinical utility and threshold transportability need further validation in larger, independent studies. The study contributes to the development of interpretable diagnostic tools for hepatitis B, emphasizing the importance of threshold-aware frameworks in clinical decision support.

title_zh: 一种结合比较可解释人工智能的贝叶斯优化异构堆叠框架用于乙型肝炎诊断支持
source_body_en: Hepatitis B diagnosis requires the combined interpretation of viral-load markers, biochemical parameters, demographic information, and clinical symptoms. Developing a reliable machine-learning model for this purpose is challenging when the available clinical dataset is small and model development involves architecture selection, hyperparameter optimization, threshold selection, and explainability analysis. This study developed Bayes Stack-HBV, a Bayesian-optimized heterogeneous stacking framework intended to provide internally validated decision support for hepatitis B classification. The framework used nine predictors comprising two hundred sixteen patient records and combined heterogeneous base learners through an Elastic Net-regularized logistic meta-learner. Model architecture and hyperparameters were optimized using 40 Optuna trials within each outer-fold training set. Performance was evaluated using repeated nested cross-validation with three random seeds, five outer folds, and three inner folds. Preprocessing, SMOTE, model optimization, and decision-threshold selection were restricted to the training and inner-validation data. Bayes Stack-HBV was compared with Default Stack-HBV, Hist Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machine, Extra Trees, Logistic Regression, and K-Nearest Neighbors. Calibration, paired statistical comparisons, and multi-method explainability analyses were performed using held-out predictions. Across 15 held-out outer-fold evaluations, Bayes Stack-HBV achieved an accuracy of 0.9337 ± 0.0324, balanced accuracy of 0.9357 ± 0.0307, precision of 0.9659 ± 0.0383, sensitivity of 0.9114 ± 0.0670, specificity of 0.9600 ± 0.0471, F1-score of 0.9357 ± 0.0331, MCC of 0.8728 ± 0.0602, ROC-AUC of 0.9844 ± 0.0162, PR-AUC of 0.9892 ± 0.0103, and Brier score of 0.0428 ± 0.0188. Bayes Stack-HBV ranked first on seven of ten mean evaluation measures, indicating a strong specificity- and calibration-oriented performance profile. However, differences relative to the strongest ensemble comparators were not statistically significant after multiple-comparison correction. Explainability analysis identified HBVDNA and ALT Level as influential predictors, supported by expanded explanation-stability and feature-dependency analyses. Bayes Stack-HBV provides promising preliminary evidence as a threshold-aware and interpretable framework for HBV decision support. Its clinical utility and threshold transportability require confirmation through larger, independent, multicenter, and prospective validation studies.
abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒(乙型肝炎病毒,HBV)的诊断需要综合解读病毒载量标志物、生化参数、人口统计信息和临床症状。当可用的临床数据集较小且模型开发涉及架构选择、超参数优化、阈值选择和可解释性分析时,开发一个可靠的机器学习模型具有挑战性。本研究开发了Bayes Stack-HBV,这是一种旨在为乙型肝炎分类提供内部验证决策支持的贝叶斯优化异构堆叠框架。该框架使用了九个预测因子,包含216份患者记录,并通过弹性网络正则化的逻辑元学习器将异构基础学习器进行组合。在每个外层折叠训练集内,使用40次Optuna试验优化模型架构和超参数。通过重复嵌套交叉验证(三个随机种子,五个外层折叠,三个内层折叠)评估模型性能。预处理、SMOTE、模型优化和决策阈值选择仅限于训练和内层验证数据。Bayes Stack-HBV与Default Stack-HBV、历史梯度提升、支持向量机、随机森林、逻辑回归和K-近邻算法进行了比较。使用保留预测进行校准、成对统计比较和多方法可解释性分析。在15次保留的外层折叠评估中,Bayes Stack-HBV达到了0.9337 ± 0.0324的准确率、0.9357 ± 0.0307的平衡准确率、0.9659 ± 0.0383的精确率、0.9114 ± 0.0670的灵敏度、0.9600 ± 0.0471的特异度、0.9357 ± 0.0331的F1分数、0.8728 ± 0.0602的MCC、0.9844 ± 0.0162的ROC-AUC、0.9892 ± 0.0103的PR-AUC以及0.0428 ± 0.0188的Brier分数。Bayes Stack-HBV在十个平均评估指标中的七个指标上排名第一,表明其具有较强的特异性和校准导向的性能特征。然而,在多重比较校正后,与最强的集成比较模型之间的差异并不具有统计学意义。可解释性分析确定了HBVDNA和ALT水平作为有影响力的预测因子,这一结论得到了扩展的解释稳定性分析和特征依赖性分析的支持。Bayes Stack-HBV作为一种阈值感知且可解释的框架,为HBV决策支持提供了有前景的初步证据。其临床实用性和阈值迁移性需要通过更大规模、独立、多中心和前瞻性验证研究来确认。

title: Interferon-Induced Protein 6 (IFI6): Biological Functions, Molecular Mechanisms and Pathological Roles in Human Diseases
abstract: Interferon (IFN)-induced protein 6 (IFI6) is an important member of the IFN-stimulated gene (ISG) family, mainly enriched in the inner mitochondrial membrane and endoplasmic reticulum (ER). It plays significant roles in anti-apoptosis, immune regulation, maintenance of mitochondrial homeostasis, antiviral defense, and promotion of tumor progression. At the molecular mechanism level, IFI6 inhibits mitochondrial membrane depolarization, cytochrome c release, and caspase activation. It also regulates the B-cell lymphoma 2 (Bcl-2)/Bcl-2 interacting mediator of cell death (Bim) expression balance, activates the janus kinase (JAK)/signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-protein kinase B (PI3K-AKT) pathways, and inhibits the degradation of ferroptosis-related proteins solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11) and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), thereby enhancing cell survival and proliferation through multiple pathways. In terms of immune regulation, IFI6 also affects immune cells (such as T/B cells, etc.) and the tumor microenvironment. IFI6 regulates mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) and mitochondrial calcium homeostasis, influencing respiratory chain assembly and metabolism. In terms of virus regulation, IFI6 may inhibit the replication of multiple viruses (such as hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), SARS-CoV-2, etc.) by inhibiting flavivirus-induced ER invagination, interfering with retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like receptor signaling pathways, and inhibiting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) kinase activity. In addition, IFI6 is highly expressed in autoimmune diseases and malignant tumors and is associated with proliferation, metastasis, and poor prognosis. In this review, we aim to highlight IFI6 as a potential key target in disease diagnosis and treatment.

title: Sexual Behaviours and Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Infection among Female Sex Workers in Lubowa Village, Wakiso District. A cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Hepatitis B virus is transmitted through parenteral contact with infected blood and sexual contact involving exposure to infectious body fluids. The study aims to assess the relationship between Sexual Behaviours and Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Infection among Female Sex Workers in Lubowa Village. Methodology The study population comprised female sex workers aged 18+ residing and operating in Lubowa Village, Wakiso District, who have been in the area for at least six consecutive months before the data collection period. Bivariate and Multivariate logistic regression were used to determine factors associated with HBV seropositivity. Statistical significance was set at p<0.05. Results Age at first sexual intercourse was significantly associated with HBV infection (χ2 = 38.04, p < 0.001). The number of sexual partners was also significantly associated with HBV infection (χ2 = 8.56, p = 0.003). Similarly, the frequency of unprotected sexual intercourse was significantly associated with HBV infection (χ2 = 10.70, p = 0.013). There was also a statistically significant association between sexual practices and HBV infection (χ2 = 42.64, p < 0.001) and between alcohol use before or during sex and HBV infection (χ2 = 8.11, p = 0.004).Most respondents were single (75.0%) and had attained primary education (57.5%). Conclusion Reducing risky sexual behaviours through comprehensive prevention, condom promotion, behavioural interventions, and targeted health education may reduce HBV transmission among female sex workers. Recommendation NGOs and peer educators should strengthen condom distribution, negotiation skills, alcohol harm reduction and economic empowerment to reduce transactional unprotected sex.
journal: Student's Journal of Health Research Africa

title: Season-adjusted longitudinal changes in serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D during pegylated interferon add-on to ongoing tenofovir alafenamide therapy in chronic hepatitis B: a real-world cohort study
abstract: Objectives To characterize serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] trajectories during peginterferon alfa-2b (Peg-IFN) add-on to ongoing tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) therapy in chronic hepatitis B and explore associations with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). Methods This retrospective cohort identified 203 consecutive patients, of whom 190 contributed longitudinal data through week 48. The primary random-intercept mixed-effects model used categorical visit time and adjusted for seasonality, age, and sex. Continuous-time, random-slope, visit-timing, and HBsAg-censoring analyses assessed sensitivity. Results The primary adjusted week-48 25(OH)D difference was −7.9 nmol/L (95% CI, −9.8 to −6.0) ( P < 0.001); the secondary continuous-time estimate was −8.3 nmol/L over 48 weeks. Observed concentrations declined through week 36 and partially rebounded at week 48. The proportion below 47.7 nmol/L increased from 21.1% to 34.7%. The adjusted total serum calcium trend was −0.061 mmol/L (95% CI, −0.074 to −0.049). Triglycerides increased while cholesterol fractions decreased. At week 48, 104/190 patients (54.7%) had an HBsAg decline of at least 1 log10 and 50/190 (26.3%) had visit-specific HBsAg loss. The concurrent 48-week change correlation was weak ( ρ = 0.150; FDR-adjusted P = 0.117), and the magnitude of 25(OH)D decline was not independently associated with either binary endpoint. Within patients, each 10 nmol/L increase in 25(OH)D was associated with a 0.068-log10 IU/mL increase in concurrent HBsAg (95% CI, 0.020 to 0.116; P = 0.006). Conclusions Serum 25(OH)D showed a non-linear decline during 48 weeks of follow-up, and the week-48 difference remained evident after adjustment for seasonality. However, without a concurrent comparator, the observed change cannot be attributed specifically to Peg-IFN, TAF, or their combination. Exploratory analyses suggested only a weak concurrent relationship between 25(OH)D and HBsAg, without evidence of prediction or causality. The clinical relevance of the observed changes in 25(OH)D and total serum calcium warrants further prospective investigation.

source_records.abstract: Objectives To characterize serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] trajectories during peginterferon alfa-2b (Peg-IFN) add-on to ongoing tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) therapy in chronic hepatitis B and explore associations with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). Methods This retrospective cohort identified 203 consecutive patients, of whom 190 contributed longitudinal data through week 48. The primary random-intercept mixed-effects model used categorical visit time and adjusted for seasonality, age, and sex. Continuous-time, random-slope, visit-timing, and HBsAg-censoring analyses assessed sensitivity. Results The primary adjusted week-48 25(OH)D difference was −7.9 nmol/L (95% CI, −9.8 to −6.0) ( P < 0.001); the secondary continuous-time estimate was −8.3 nmol/L over 48 weeks. Observed concentrations declined through week 36 and partially rebounded at week 48. The proportion below 47.7 nmol/L increased from 21.1% to 34.7%. The adjusted total serum calcium trend was −0.061 mmol/L (95% CI, −0.074 to −0.049). Triglycerides increased while cholesterol fractions decreased. At week 48, 104/190 patients (54.7%) had an HBsAg decline of at least 1 log10 and 50/190 (26.3%) had visit-specific HBsAg loss. The concurrent 48-week change correlation was weak ( ρ = 0.150; FDR-adjusted P = 0.117), and the magnitude of 25(OH)D decline was not independently associated with either binary endpoint. Within patients, each 10 nmol/L increase in 25(OH)D was associated with a 0.068-log10 IU/mL increase in concurrent HBsAg (95% CI, 0.020 to 0.116; P = 0.006). Conclusions Serum 25(OH)D showed a non-linear decline during 48 weeks of follow-up, and the week-48 difference remained evident after adjustment for seasonality. However, without a concurrent comparator, the observed change cannot be attributed specifically to Peg-IFN, TAF, or their combination. Exploratory analyses suggested only a weak concurrent relationship between 25(OH)D and HBsAg, without evidence of prediction or causality. The clinical relevance of the observed changes in 25(OH)D and total serum calcium warrants further prospective investigation.

title: Risk-based hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance thresholds using a prediction score in Asian patients with chronic hepatitis B: a nationwide cohort study
abstract: Background/Aims: This study aimed to quantify hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence according to a validated prediction score and to define score-based cut-offs corresponding to surveillance-relevant incidence thresholds in Asian patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) receiving antiviral therapy.Methods: We conducted a nationwide population-based cohort study using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Adults with CHB initiating nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy between 2012 and 2023 were included; those with viral coinfections, prior malignancy, or decompensated cirrhosis were excluded. HCC risk was stratified using the HCC-RESCUE score. Incident HCC was the primary outcome. title: The Influence Of Education Through Animated Video Media On Pregnant Women's Knowledge And Attitudes About Triple Elimination Screening (HIV, Syphilis, And Hepatitis B) At The Gerungang Public Health Center
abstract: Triple Elimination screening is a public health program designed to prevent the transmission of HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B from pregnant women to their babies. According to data from the Gerunggang Community Health Center in Pangkal Pinang, the coverage rate for Triple Elimination screening among pregnant women decreased from 43.8% (2023) to 41.7% (2024), while the rate of reactive test results increased from 7% to 9%. This study aimed to determine the effect of education via animated video on the knowledge and attitudes of pregnant women regarding triple elimination screening in the Gerunggang Community Health Center’s service area in 2026, using a quasi-experimental, non-equivalent control group, pretest-posttest design with 19 respondents in the intervention group and 19 in the control group. Univariate analysis results showed that before the education program, nearly all pregnant women (84.2%) in the intervention group had insufficient knowledge and the majority (63.2%) held negative attitudes, whereas after the education program, nearly all (89.5%) had good knowledge and nearly all (94.7%) held positive attitudes, while in the control group, the changes observed were relatively minor. The results of the Wilcoxon test in the intervention group showed p=0.001 for knowledge and p=0.001 for attitudes, while the Mann-Whitney posttest showed p=0.001 for knowledge and p=0.000 for attitudes, indicating significant differences between the two groups. It was concluded that education through animated videos has a significant impact on the knowledge and attitudes of pregnant women therefore, it is recommended that the Gerunggang Community Health Center incorporate this medium as a routine health promotion strategy in its antenatal care (ANC) services.

title: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Hepatitis B Among Women of Reproductive Age in Obio Akpor Local Government Area
abstract: The Hepatitis B virus (HBV) has remained a major public health challenge particularly in Nigeria. The study aimed to assess the prevalence and risk factors of HBV among women of reproductive age attending primary health care facilities in Obio/Apkor LGA. The study adopted a facility-based cross-sectional design and data from 346 respondents were collected across 7 primary health centers from January – March 2025. Data was collected via semi structured questionnaire using a simple random sampling technique while a rapid diagnostic test strip (Popular, one step strip style and jell) was used to screen for Hepatitis B virus. Data collected was analyzed using chi-square, bivariate and multivariate analysis (SPSS vs 26) with statistical significance set at p>0.05 at 95% confidence interval. The result showed a high level of knowledge, attitude and perception (KAP) towards Hepatitis B disease. The majority (64.5%) showed good knowledge, 80.9% showed positive attitude and 90.2% showed positive perception. Socio-demographic variables such as education, employment status and income were significantly associated with knowledge and attitude while pregnancy status and parity were associated with perceptions. The result revealed a total prevalence of 11(3.2%) 95% (Cl: 1.35-5.04) with higher prevalence among women aged 27-32 years 5(4.3%), married women 8(3.1%), those with secondary education 5(3%) and self-employed 6(3.4%). Key risk factors identified in this study included delivery at traditional birth attendant (aOR=6.613, Cl: 1.40 31.26), shared razor/needles (aOR=4.665, Cl: 1.09-19.92) and polygamous marriage (aOR=4.928, Cl: 1.04-23.23). The findings revealed a moderate level of Hepatitis B prevalence among the study population. It is recommended that sensitization on health education may reduce the transmission of Hepatitis B Virus.

title: Two-Decade Evaluation of Pediatric Hepatitis B Immunization: Shifting Immune Kinetics and Metabolic/Clinical Predictors of Vaccine Non-Response

title: Resolved hepatitis B is associated with higher reactivation risk than chronic infection after chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: BACKGROUND Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a cornerstone treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation risk, particularly among patients with prior infection, remains incompletely characterized, with international guidelines providing discordant risk classifications. We hypothesized that patients with resolved HBV infection undergoing TACE face a higher reactivation risk than currently estimated by international guidelines. AIM To determine the incidence and risk factors of HBV reactivation in patients undergoing TACE for HBV-related HCC. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent TACE for HBV-related HCC at a tertiary hospital during 2007-2025. Patients receiving baseline antiviral therapy were excluded. Patients with definitive serostatus (n = 774) were stratified into chronic-infection [hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive, n = 727] and resolved-infection (HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive, n = 47) groups. Cumulative incidences and risk factors were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression, with robustness evaluated through multiple imputation, competing-risks, and antiviral-naive sensitivity analyses. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 16.7 months, HBV reactivation occurred in 60 patients (6.1% overall). Patients with resolved HBV status had a higher reactivation rate (21.3% vs 6.9%; P CONCLUSION HBV reactivation occurred in approximately 6% of patients undergoing TACE, with resolved infection status conferring > 3-fold higher risk and reactivation incidence exceeding 20%. These findings support prophylactic antiviral therapy rather than monitoring alone for HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive patients undergoing TACE.

title: Hepatitis B Vaccination Intention and Influencing Factors among College Students in Huanggang, Hubei, China: A Protection Motivation Theory-Based Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Objective: This study assessed the intention to receive the hepatitis B vaccine and identified influencing factors among college students in Huanggang, China, using the Protection Motivation Theory (PMT).Material and Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted between April and May 2025. Data were collected via PMT-based questionnaire measuring knowledge, preventive behaviors, perceived severity, perceived susceptibility, response efficacy, self-efficacy, and response cost. Statistical analyses were performed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) v27.0 to examine associations between variables and vaccination intention.Results: Among the 1,130 participants, 58.9% intended to receive the hepatitis B vaccine. In bivariate analyses, higher hepatitis B knowledge, vaccine knowledge, preventive behaviors, and favorable PMT constructs were positively associated with intention. Multivariate logistic regression confirmed independent associations: hepatitis B knowledge (odds ratio [OR]=1.41, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.02-1.95), vaccine knowledge (OR=1.49, 95% CI: 1.11-2.00), preventive behaviors (OR=1.60, 95% CI: 1.15-2.23), perceived severity (OR=1.05, 95% CI: 1.01-1.10), self-efficacy (OR=1.10, 95% CI: 1.02-1.18), and response efficacy (OR=1.16, 95% CI: 1.04-1.29) were positive predictors, whereas perceived response cost (OR=0.85, 95% CI: 0.79-0.91) was a negative predictor. Sociodemographic factors were not significant after adjustment.Conclusion: The findings offer insights into hepatitis B vaccination behavior among college students. This evidence-based information could inform the future direction for improving hepatitis B vaccination rates in university settings by focusing health education on the severity of the hepatitis B consequences and the efficacy and safety of the vaccination, all of which could reduce the psychological and practical barriers.

title: Hubungan Determinan Sosial Kesehatan dengan Ketepatan Waktu Skrining Hepatitis B pada Ibu Hamil
abstract: Hepatitis B masih menjadi masalah kesehatan masyarakat karena berisiko tinggi ditularkan dari ibu ke bayi, sehingga skrining pada trimester pertama kehamilan sangat penting. Ketepatan waktu skrining di wilayah kerja Puskesmas Sukaraja Nuban, Lampung Timur, masih rendah (21,6%). Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan determinan sosial kesehatan dengan ketepatan waktu skrining Hepatitis B pada ibu hamil. Penelitian analitik observasional dengan desain case control dilakukan pada Juli–Desember 2025 terhadap 76 ibu hamil (38 skrining tepat waktu dan 38 tidak tepat waktu) yang dipilih secara simple random sampling. Variabel pendapatan, pendidikan, status pekerjaan, dan keterpaparan informasi kesehatan dianalisis dengan uji chi-square/Fisher's exact dan Odds Ratio (OR). Pendapatan (p = 1,00) dan status pekerjaan (p = 1,00) tidak berhubungan dengan ketepatan waktu skrining. Pendidikan (p = 0,007; OR = 0,18; IK 95% 0,05–0,61) dan keterpaparan informasi (p = 0,021; OR = 3,32; IK 95% 1,29–8,54) berhubungan secara bermakna. Ibu berpendidikan tinggi justru lebih jarang melakukan skrining tepat waktu, sedangkan ibu dengan keterpaparan informasi tinggi berpeluang 3,3 kali lebih besar melakukan skrining tepat waktu. Penguatan penyampaian informasi kesehatan sejak kunjungan antenatal pertama, tanpa memandang latar belakang pendidikan, diperlukan untuk meningkatkan ketepatan waktu skrining Hepatitis B.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Rapid Diagnostic Tests Versus Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) Across Major Infectious Diseases: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) are increasingly used for point-of-care diagnosis of infectious diseases because of their rapid turnaround time and ease of use.However, their diagnostic performance compared with enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) varies across diseases and assay platforms.This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines.A total of 26 studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, of which 13 datasets from 11 studies with complete 2 × 2 diagnostic data were included in the meta-analysis.Quality assessment was performed using QUADAS-2 (Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2).Pooled diagnostic performance was summarized separately for each infection using extracted true-positive (TP), false-positive (FP), true-negative (TN), and false-negative (FN) values; forest plots, an HSROC (Hierarchical Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic model)-style summary visualization, and a Deeks-type funnel plot were generated.The aggregate diagnostic counts were TP = 1,304, FP = 68, TN = 24,301, and FN = 303.Overall, the included datasets showed consistently high specificity (≥96.97%),whereas sensitivity varied widely (25%-100%) across conditions.By target condition, the pooled sensitivity and specificity were human immunodeficiency virus (HIV; 78.6%/99.30%),hepatitis B virus (HBV; 88.2%/99.94%),hepatitis C virus (HCV; 75.7%/99.42%),dengue (97.0%/99.97%),and malaria (100.0%/97.18%).RDTs demonstrated high specificity and good sensitivity compared with ELISA, supporting their role as rapid screening tools, particularly in resource-limited settings.However, heterogeneity across diseases and assay platforms limits generalizability, and confirmatory testing remains important in selected clinical and blood-screening settings.

title: Threshold Geometry, Bifurcation, and Data-Driven Analysis of a Vaccination-Treatment Model for Hepatitis B
abstract: Despite the availability of excellent vaccines and antiviral medicines, hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major public health problem. In this work, we develop a mathematical vaccination-treatment model for HBV transmission to investigate threshold conditions for illness persistence as well as the level of intervention. The analysis gives the characterisation of both disease-free and endemic equilibria and determines the basic reproduction number, $\mathcal{R}_0$, by the next-generation matrix approach. The model indicates that $\mathcal{R}_0=1$ is a critical threshold dividing disease-free from endemic states and characterises a forward transcritical bifurcation regarding the transmission parameter. Numerical equilibrium continuation and stability assessments confirm the analytical results. A two-parameter study of transmission and vaccination rates identifies threshold geometries and assesses impacts of important parameters using sensitivity analysis. The model is calibrated with India-specific data, such as HBsAg prevalence, HBV incidence and mortality rates and fits epidemiological targets closely through limited nonlinear calibration. Additionally, multi-start optimisation and practical identifiability profiling are used to investigate parameter uncertainty. Robustness analyses reveal that the calibrated $\mathcal{R}_0^*=1.1744$ is associated with a super-threshold regime; however, parameter flexibility permits both sub-threshold and super-threshold regimes. This combined analytical and data-driven framework connects epidemic thresholds, bifurcation structures, intervention efficacy, and parameter uncertainty. It provides a quantitative framework for analysing HBV persistence and evaluating control options, especially in the absence of epidemiological evidence.

title: Prevalence of Anaemia, Fasting Hyperglycaemia and Hepatitis B Surface Antigenaemia among Pregnant Women Attending a Tertiary Hospital in Owerri, South-East Nigeria
abstract: Background: Anaemia, hyperglycaemia first detected in pregnancy and hepatitis B virus infection are important, largely detectable conditions that can adversely affect maternal and neonatal health. Evidence describing their burden within the same antenatal population in South-East Nigeria remains limited. Objective: This study determined the prevalence of anaemia, fasting hyperglycaemia meeting the World Health Organization gestational diabetes threshold, and hepatitis B surface antigenaemia among pregnant women attending the Federal University Teaching Hospital, Owerri, Imo State, Nigeria, and compared prevalence across trimesters. Methods: A hospital-based descriptive cross-sectional study enrolled 300 consenting pregnant women by consecutive sampling, with 100 women in each trimester. Venous blood was collected into ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, fluoride-oxalate and plain tubes. Packed cell volume was measured by the microhaematocrit method and haemoglobin concentration was estimated as packed cell volume divided by three. Fasting plasma glucose was determined by the glucose oxidase method. Hepatitis B surface antigen was screened by immunochromatography, with reactive specimens confirmed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Anaemia was defined as haemoglobin <11.0 g/dL, while fasting hyperglycaemia was defined as glucose ≥92 mg/dL. Prevalence estimates were reported with 95% Wilson confidence intervals; trimester differences were examined using Pearson's chi-square test. title: Predictive model to identify patients requiring extended interferon therapy in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: A contemporary study by Yan et al , published in the World Journal of Gastroen terology , demonstrates that baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis can be utilized in a prediction model to identify populations that may benefit from extended (≥ 48 weeks) interferon therapy. In this editorial, we summarize strengths of their study. First, the follow-up period was sufficiently long; second, the authors identified all major confounding factors; third, appropriate statistical methods were employed; fourth, the figures and tables are highly legible; and fifth, the training cohort exhibited stable discriminatory ability. The limitations of the study are as follows: First, the sample size in certain subgroups was too small; second, nearly all similar studies have been conducted in China, leaving readers with a limited understanding of global trends in this field; and third, the benefits of adding PEGylated interferon α-2b to nucleos(t)ide analog therapy were not addressed. Future research should investigate the promising role of combination therapies involving PEGylated interferon α-2b and nucleos(t)ide analogs, incorporate machine learning approaches, and consider the effects of concurrent nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.

title: Age-Specific Prevalence and Vulnerability to Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Infection in Kaura Namoda, Nigeria
abstract: Age is a crucial factor in the transmission and development of infectious illnesses; nevertheless, age-specific patterns in Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) incidence remain little investigated in rural Nigerian populations. This research analyses the age-stratified prevalence of HBV cases in the Kaura Namoda Local Government Area, Zamfara State, Nigeria, utilising hospital-based data from 2019 to 2023. Confirmed HBV cases were classified into three age categories: children (0– 9 years), teenagers (10–19 years), and adults (20 years and older). Analysis of secondary data from Kauran Namoda General Hospital indicated that the adult demographic exhibited the highest prevalence, succeeded by teenagers, whilst children demonstrated the lowest infection rates. The low incidence among children is probably attributable to the efficacy of Nigeria's standard baby immunisation initiatives. Nonetheless, adolescents and adults—many of whom were born before to the advent of mass vaccination—continue to be susceptible due to occupational exposure, customary practices employing unsterilised tools, and restricted access to catch-up immunisation. These findings highlight the necessity of broadening HBV control methods beyond paediatric immunisation. The report advocates for age-specific treatments, including health education aimed at adolescents in schools, mobile outreach services for adults, and the incorporation of HBV immunisation into workplace health programs. Catch-up immunisation initiatives must be expanded to address immunity deficiencies in older demographics. Comprehending the varying impact of HBV across age groups is crucial for attaining equitable and thorough disease management. This study provides critical insights to guide targeted, age-responsive interventions designed to mitigate HBV transmission and attain eradication objectives in high-risk rural communities.

title: From virological selection to immune stratification: Hepatitis B virus-specific T cells for precision pegylated interferon therapy in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Pegylated interferon (PEG-IFN) alpha, an important agent for chronic hepatitis B (CHB), exerts antiviral and immunomodulatory activities and serves as a core therapy to pursue functional cure. However, there are significant individual differences in treatment response, and the lack of reliable patient-selection strategies remains a major limitation to clinical application. Recent studies have shown that hepatitis B virus (HBV)-specific T cells are the core effector cells mediating viral clearance and maintaining immune control, and that the degree of their functional restoration is closely related to responses to PEG-IFN treatment and hepatitis B surface antigen clearance. In chronic HBV infection, HBV-specific T cells generally exhibit characteristics such as reduced numbers, functional exhaustion, metabolic abnormalities, and epigenetic remodeling. PEG-IFN can achieve immune remodeling by enhancing HBV-specific T cell responses, promoting the formation of memory-like T cells, improving multifunctional effector functions, and partially reversing the exhausted state. This review summarizes HBV-specific T cell dysfunction in chronic HBV infection, PEG-IFN-mediated immune remodeling mechanisms and relevant biomarker advances, to discuss the value of these T cells for precise interferon candidate screening and immune-stratified therapy. Such indicators may transform CHB management from virology-based to immunology-guided strategies and support precision treatment toward functional cure.

title: A case of Atypical Occult Hepatitis B Infection (OBI) with HBsAg Negativity and High Anti-HBs Titer: Clinical implications
abstract: A 72-year-old male patient was admitted presenting with upper abdominal distension and pain for one day. He had a 20-year history of hypertension and a 10-year history of hepatitis B, which he reported had been cured. Laboratory tests revealed a distinctive serological profile characterized by HBsAg negativity, anti-HBs positivity (714.2 mIU/ml), anti-HBe positivity, and anti-HBc positivity. However, HBV DNA was tested positive (5.962×102 IU/mL). The imaging studies revealed a heterogeneous space-occupying lesion in the left hepatic lobe. This case challenges the conventional perception that “a high anti-HBs titer is indicative of protective immunity and successful viral clearance”. The patient underwent resection of the lesion and received regular follow-up postoperatively.

title: Semi-quantitative ultrasound scoring reveals hepatic structural recovery and immune modulation during tenofovir alafenamide therapy in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system, and to investigate the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. Methods A total of 100 CHB patients who received TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) for at least 24 months were retrospectively enrolled. A seven-parameter semi-quantitative US score, encompassing liver echogenicity, capsular contour, margin shape, vessel clarity, portal vein diameter (PVD), spleen thickness (ST), and splenic vein velocity (SVV), was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Concurrently, serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), peripheral T-cell subsets, including cluster of differentiation 3-positive (CD3 + ), CD4 + , CD8 + T cells, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were measured. Correlations between US scores and biochemical/immune parameters were analyzed. Results At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The comprehensive US score decreased significantly from 7.86 ± 1.73 at baseline to 3.37 ± 0.95 at 24 months ( P < 0.001), with the most pronounced improvements observed in capsular smoothness and parenchymal homogeneity. The CD4 + T-cell proportion and CD4 + /CD8 + ratio increased, whereas the CD8 + proportion decreased; NK cell activity rose from 42.7 ± 7.3% to 52.4 ± 6.2% ( P < 0.05). The US score was positively correlated with ALT (r = 0.56) and AST (r = 0.47), and negatively correlated with the CD4 + /CD8 + ratio (r = −0.46) and NK cell activity (r = −0.38) (all P < 0.01). Conclusion These findings indicate that TAF not only suppresses viral replication and normalises liver enzymes but also promotes measurable structural liver improvement, as reflected by declining semi-quantitative US scores. The strong correlations of US scores with biochemical and immune parameters support its utility as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在利用半定量超声(US)评分系统评估替诺福韦艾拉酚胺二甲基磺酸盐(TAF)在慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者中的治疗反应,并探讨超声影像变化与免疫功能恢复之间的相关性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 入选了100例接受TAF单药治疗(25 mg/天)至少24个月的慢性乙型肝炎患者进行回顾性分析。研究持续时间为24个月,在基线、12个月和24个月时计算超声评分。
elements_zh.methods: 计算了包含肝脏回声、包膜轮廓、边缘形态、血管清晰度、门静脉直径(PVD)、脾脏厚度(ST)和脾静脉血流速度(SVV)的七参数半定量超声评分。同时测量了血清乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)脱氧核糖核酸(DNA)、丙氨酸氨基转移酶(ALT)、天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶(AST)以及外周T细胞亚群,包括分化簇3阳性(CD3+)、CD4+、CD8+ T细胞、CD4+/CD8+比值和自然杀伤(NK)细胞活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 在24个月时,所有患者均达到HBV DNA <20 IU/mL,ALT和AST的正常化率分别为92%和95%。综合超声评分从基线的7.86 ± 1.73显著下降至24个月的3.37 ± 0.95(P < 0.001),其中包膜平滑度和实质均匀性的改善最为显著。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,TAF不仅抑制病毒复制并使肝酶正常化,还促进可测量的肝脏结构改善,这体现在半定量超声评分的下降。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的强相关性支持其作为非侵入性影像生物标志物用于监测治疗疗效和肝脏修复的潜力。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计和可能存在的选择偏倚,但由于观察到了显著的统计结果和明确的相关性,其证据是强有力的。

title_zh: 半定量超声评分揭示慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)在接受替诺福韦艾拉酚胺治疗期间肝脏结构恢复和免疫调节
source_body_en: Objective This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system, and to investigate the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. Methods A total of 100 CHB patients who received TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) for at least 24 months were retrospectively enrolled. A seven-parameter semi-quantitative US score, encompassing liver echogenicity, capsular contour, margin shape, vessel clarity, portal vein diameter (PVD), spleen thickness (ST), and splenic vein velocity (SVV), was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Concurrently, serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), peripheral T-cell subsets, including cluster of differentiation 3-positive (CD3 + ), CD4 + , CD8 + T cells, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were measured. Correlations between US scores and biochemical/immune parameters were analyzed. Results At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The comprehensive US score decreased significantly from 7.86 ± 1.73 at baseline to 3.37 ± 0.95 at 24 months ( P < 0.001), with the most pronounced improvements observed in capsular smoothness and parenchymal homogeneity. The CD4 + T-cell proportion and CD4 + /CD8 + ratio increased, whereas the CD8 + proportion decreased; NK cell activity rose from 42.7 ± 7.3% to 52.4 ± 6.2% ( P < 0.05). The US score was positively correlated with ALT (r = 0.56) and AST (r = 0.47), and negatively correlated with the CD4 + /CD8 + ratio (r = −0.46) and NK cell activity (r = −0.38) (all P < 0.01). Conclusion These findings indicate that TAF not only suppresses viral replication and normalises liver enzymes but also promotes measurable structural liver improvement, as reflected by declining semi-quantitative US scores. The strong correlations of US scores with biochemical and immune parameters support its utility as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在利用半定量超声(US)评分系统评估替诺福韦艾拉酚胺二甲基磺酸盐(TAF)在慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者中的治疗反应,并探讨超声影像变化与免疫功能恢复之间的相关性。方法 入选了100例接受TAF单药治疗(25 mg/天)至少24个月的慢性乙型肝炎患者进行回顾性分析。在基线、12个月和24个月时计算了包含肝脏回声、包膜轮廓、边缘形态、血管清晰度、门静脉直径(PVD)、脾脏厚度(ST)和脾静脉血流速度(SVV)的七参数半定量超声评分。同时测量了血清乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)脱氧核糖核酸(DNA)、丙氨酸氨基转移酶(ALT)、天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶(AST)以及外周T细胞亚群,包括分化簇3阳性(CD3+)、CD4+、CD8+ T细胞、CD4+/CD8+比值和自然杀伤(NK)细胞活性。分析了超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的相关性。结果 在24个月时,所有患者均达到HBV DNA <20 IU/mL,ALT和AST的正常化率分别为92%和95%。综合超声评分从基线的7.86 ± 1.73显著下降至24个月的3.37 ± 0.95(P < 0.001),其中包膜平滑度和实质均匀性的改善最为显著。CD4+ T细胞比例和CD4+/CD8+比值增加,而CD8+ T细胞比例下降;NK细胞活性从42.7 ± 7.3%上升至52.4 ± 6.2%(P < 0.05)。超声评分与ALT(r = 0.56)和AST(r = 0.47)呈正相关,与CD4+/CD8+比值(r = −0.46)和NK细胞活性(r = −0.38)呈负相关(所有P < 0.01)。结论 这些发现表明,TAF不仅抑制病毒复制并使肝酶正常化,还促进可测量的肝脏结构改善,这体现在半定量超声评分的下降。超声评分与生化和免疫参数之间的强相关性支持其作为非侵入性影像生物标志物用于监测治疗疗效和肝脏修复的潜力。

title: Clonorchis sinensis co-infection potentiates polymorphonuclear-myeloid-derived suppressor cells expansion and metabolic reprogramming in chronic hepatitis B patients
abstract: BACKGROUND Clonorchis sinensis (C. sinensis ) co-infection is known to accelerate disease progression and induce immune tolerance in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV), particularly in regions where both infections are endemic. Metabolic reprogramming has emerged as a key driver of immunosuppression. These metabolic shifts are often orchestrated by myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), which expand during chronic infections to promote immune tolerance. sinensis co-infection reprograms metabolism to favor MDSC-linked suppression and how this process relates to normal liver enzyme levels remains unclear. AIM To investigate whether C. sinensis co-infection induces MDSC- linked metabolic reprogramming in patients with HBV and normal liver enzyme levels. METHODS In this cross-sectional study, a total of 117 participants were enrolled and assigned to four groups: Healthy controls (n = 30), C. sinensis mono-infected participants (n = 29), HBV mono-infected participants (n = 28), and co-infected participants (n = 30). Serum cytokine profiles were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, amino acid metabolites using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and MDSC subsets using flow cytometry. Spearman correlation and mediation analyses were performed to explore the relationships among inflammation, metabolism, and immunity. RESULTS HBV mono-infected and co-infected patients showed no statistically significant differences in liver enzyme and HBV DNA levels. However, compared with the HBV mono-infected group, the co-infected group had higher levels of the inflammatory cytokine: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), accompanied by markedly lower interferon-γ (IFN-γ) levels. Flow cytometric assay revealed that polymorphonuclear MDSCs (PMN-MDSCs) showed the greatest expansion in the co-infected group, and their proportion correlated strongly with IL-6 and TNF-α levels. Metabolically, the co-infected group had a significantly higher ornithine-to-arginine ratio. Mediation analysis suggested that PMN-MDSCs accounted for approximately 45% of the total effect of IL-6 on IFN-γ suppression. sinensis co-infection was associated with immunosuppression through IL-6/TNF-α-linked PMN-MDSC expansion and elevated ornithine-to-arginine ratio, resulting in suppressed IFN-γ production despite normal liver enzyme levels.

title: Interferon-λ receptor positive monocytes/macrophages orchestrate a pro-fibrotic immune environment in hepatitis B virus-related liver fibrosis
abstract: Abstract Interferon-λ receptor (IFNLR), a heterodimer composed of IFNLR1 and IL-10Rβ, mediates IFN-λ-driven fibrotic effects. This study investigated the involvement of IFNLR1+ monocytes/macrophages in orchestrating pro-fibrotic immune microenvironment. Flow cytometric analysis of peripheral blood showed that IFNLR1+ monocytes were elevated in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection (CHI) and patients with HBV-related liver cirrhosis (LC), compared with healthy controls (HC). These cells also displayed a CCR2hiCCR5hiCX3CR1hiCD86hiHLA-DRhiCD163hiMERTKhi phenotype with an IL-10hiTNF-αhi cytokine profile. Hepatic fibrosis was induced in wild-type and Ifnlr1-knockout (Ifnlr1−/−) mice using carbon tetrachloride and recombinant adeno-associated virus 8-1.3HBV. Ifnlr1 deficiency down-regulated CCR2 and CCR5 expression on monocytes/macrophages, attenuated collagen deposition, but enhanced HBV–DNA replication. In vitro, bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) were co-cultured with hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) or naive CD4+ T cells to assess the functional impact of IFNLR1+ macrophages. Concurrently, the involvement of lipid metabolism in IFN-λ/IFNLR1-mediated macrophage regulation was examined using liver X receptor (LXR) agonists/antagonists. Ifnlr1−/− BMDMs exhibited a diminished capacity to activate HSCs and drive regulatory T cells differentiation. Mechanistically, IFN-λ–IFNLR1 signaling suppressed LXR-dependent lipid metabolism, thereby promoting tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α and IL-1β production, and LXR pathway inhibition favored M1-macrophage polarization. Collectively, IFNLR1 identifies a pro-fibrotic and immunoregulatory monocyte/macrophage subset. Targeting IFNLR1–LXR axis may represent promising anti-fibrotic strategies for HBV-related liver fibrosis.

title: Chronic viral hepatitis with concurrent metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: dual etiology challenges
abstract: The overlapping epidemics of chronic viral hepatitis and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) present a complex challenge in modern hepatology. In chronic hepatitis B, a unique “steatosis paradox” emerges: while isolated hepatic steatosis provides a suppressive microenvironment that promotes hepatitis B viral clearance, the concomitant systemic cardiometabolic burden acts dose-dependently to drive fibrogenesis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Conversely, chronic hepatitis C and host metabolic dysfunctions exhibit synergistic destruction. Hepatitis C virus actively hijacks lipid metabolism and induces insulin resistance. Even after viral eradication via direct-acting antivirals, residual steatosis and glycemic abnormalities remain formidable drivers of HCC. Consequently, the traditional virocentric paradigm is no longer sufficient. Clinical management should pivot toward precision risk stratification and a multidisciplinary dual-target approach, equally prioritizing sustained viral suppression and aggressive metabolic remission. This review summarizes the divergent virus-MASLD interactions, optimal clinical strategies, current challenges and future opportunities.

title: Sex, Drugs, and the Language of Donor Narratives: Associations With Kidney Acceptance.
abstract: Background: Despite the shortage of donor kidneys, nonutilization remains common. We hypothesized that social history language in donor narratives influences acceptance. Using Natural Language Processing, we evaluated how language describing high-risk behaviors interacts with objective data (eg, hepatitis B virus [HBV]/hepatitis C virus [HCV] testing) to affect kidney acceptance. Methods: We queried the Standard Transplant Analysis and Research file (2007-2023), analyzing 151 591 donor narratives with Natural Language Processing to identify 40 topics grouped as Templated Administrative Content and Free-Text Clinical Descriptors. Free-Text Clinical Descriptors were further subdivided into 4 communities, including Social History. Modified Poisson regression modeled associations with acceptance across 3 eras (2007-2014, 2015-2020, 2021-2023), including interactions with HBV/HCV serology. Results: Of 151 591 potential donors, 122 106 (80.55%) were accepted. Positive HBV/HCV testing reduced acceptance in era 1 (risk ratio [RR], 0.773; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.744-0.802), with attenuation in era 2 (RR, 0.893; 95% CI, 0.878-0.908), and no effect in era 3 (RR, 1.006; 95% CI, 0.993-1.019). Interactions between HBV/HCV positivity and topics reflecting language related to illicit drug use or infectious risk evaluation were associated with reduced acceptance in era 1 only, with no significant interaction in era 2 or era 3. In era 1, interaction terms indicated reduced acceptance for language describing illicit drug use and/or sex in exchange for drugs (RR, 0.665; 95% CI, 0.549-0.805) and infectious risk evaluation (RR, 0.640; 95% CI, 0.452-0.905). Conclusions: The association between high-risk behavioral language and lower kidney acceptance was present in earlier eras but not in the modern era. These findings suggest that the influence of subjective narrative language on decision-making has diminished over time, consistent with advances in antiviral therapy, policy changes, and increased utilization of higher-risk donors.

title: HBV and HIV Infections Among Pregnant Women Attending Antenatal Care at the Health Facilities In Ekiti South, Nigeria
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) are major blood-borne infections with significant motherto-child transmission potential, posing a high burden in sub-Saharan Africa. This cross-sectional study determined the prevalence of HBV, HCV, and HIV among pregnant women attending health facilities in Ekiti State, Nigeria. A total of 710 pregnant women were recruited from six Local Government Areas (Ekiti South West, Ikere, Ise, Emure, Ekiti East, and Gbonyin LGAs). Socio-demographic data and information on knowledge, awareness, and attitudes were gathered using a structured questionnaire. Venous blood specimens were collected aseptically and screened for HBsAg, anti-HCV, and HIV antibodies. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to analyze prevalence and associations (p 0.05). The study revealed an intermediate endemicity level of HBV infection among pregnant women in Ekiti South Senatorial District. Strengthening antenatal screening programmes, improving community awareness, and expanding HBV vaccination coverage, particularly among populations with lower educational attainment and in higher-prevalence LGAs, may contribute substantially to achieving the elimination targets for viral hepatitis.

title: HBV/HCV coinfection and anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury: from risk assessment and exploration of mechanisms to preventive considerations
abstract: PURPOSE: Anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (AT-DILI) is a common and clinically significant adverse event during tuberculosis treatment. Previous studies have frequently reported an increased risk of AT-DILI among patients coinfected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) and/or hepatitis C virus (HCV). This review aims to explore potential mechanisms underlying this heightened susceptibility and to discuss prevention considerations for patients with tuberculosis and HBV/HCV coinfection. METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, supplemented by clinical guidelines and authoritative reports, to identify relevant studies published through August 2026. Relevant articles were screened and thematically organized to synthesize evidence on risk estimation, underlying mechanisms, and prevention considerations. RESULTS: Available evidence indicates that HBV/HCV coinfection is associated with increased AT-DILI risk, with the magnitude varying by viral activity, baseline liver disease, and virological indicator selection. Higher viral loads appear more closely associated with AT-DILI risk. Potential mechanisms include immune-inflammatory changes, altered drug metabolism, reduced hepatic reserve, and virus-specific liver injury, including HBV reactivation. These observations inform preventive strategies targeting these risks and potential mechanisms, including baseline hepatic and virological assessment, dynamic monitoring, antiviral therapy, individualized anti-tuberculosis regimen optimization, and selective use of hepatoprotective agents. CONCLUSION: HBV/HCV coinfection increases the risk of AT-DILI and warrants active clinical attention. Future efforts should focus on individualizing prevention based on virological and hepatic status, while validating emerging biomarkers and artificial intelligence-based predictive tools to refine risk identification.

abstract_zh: 目的:抗结核药物引起的肝损伤(AT-DILI)是结核病 治疗 期间常见且具有临床意义的不良事件。先前的研究经常报告,同时感染 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 和/或丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 的患者发生 AT-DILI 的风险增加。本综述旨在探讨这种易感性升高的潜在机制,并讨论结核病和 HBV/HCV 合并感染患者的预防注意事项。方法:我们在 PubMed、Web of Science 和 Google Scholar 上进行了全面的文献检索,并辅以临床指南和权威报告,以确定截至 2026 年 8 月发表的相关研究。筛选并按主题组织相关文章,以综合有关风险估计、潜在机制和预防考虑因素的证据。结果:现有证据表明 HBV/HCV 合并感染与 AT-DILI 风险增加相关,其程度因病毒活动、基线肝病和病毒学指标选择而异。较高的病毒载量似乎与 AT-DILI 风险更密切相关。潜在的机制包括免疫炎症变化、药物代谢改变、肝储备减少和病毒特异性肝损伤,包括 HBV 再激活。这些观察结果为针对这些风险和潜在机制的预防策略提供了信息,包括基线肝脏和病毒学评估、动态监测、抗病毒药物治疗、个体化抗结核方案优化以及选择性使用保肝药物。结论:HBV/HCV 合并感染会增加 AT-DILI 的风险,值得临床积极关注。未来的努力应侧重于基于病毒学和肝脏状况的个体化预防,同时验证新兴生物标志物和基于人工智能的预测工具以完善风险识别。

title: A multicenter multistate modeling on the natural history of liver decompensation: Longitudinal analysis of 1777 patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cirrhosis often remains silent until decompensation, after which survival deteriorates sharply. Contemporary, transition-aware estimates are limited, especially in Asian-predominant cohorts. We analyzed trajectories from compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) through sequential decompensations to death. METHOD: In this multicenter study, we analyzed retrospective data from an adult cohort with liver stiffness ≥15 kPa from vibration-controlled transient elastography across 19 institutions internationally. Decompensation included ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, or variceal bleeding. Multistate models were constructed to characterize patient trajectories across 4 main clinically meaningful states: baseline cACLD, first decompensation, a subsequent second decompensation, and death. Etiology-specific subgroup analyses were conducted, and the effects of univariable predictors on transitions were also examined. RESULTS: Among 1777 patients, 265 (14.9%) developed a first decompensation over a median follow-up of 4.25 years. In the main multistate analysis cohort, from baseline cACLD, first decompensation occurred in 215 patients at 3.10 per 100 person-years, while death occurred at a rate of 1.01 per 100 person-years. The rate of a second decompensation was higher following the first decompensation, at 42.73 per 100 person-years. Patients with alcohol-associated liver disease had the highest rate of progression from baseline to first decompensation, whereas patients with hepatitis B etiology had the lowest progression rate into a second decompensation following a first decompensating event. CONCLUSION: Most patients with cACLD remain compensated over 10 years of follow-up, but once decompensation occurs, trajectories accelerate, and survival worsens. Transition-aware, etiology-stratified estimates enable individualized prognostication and earlier risk-guided intervention, including timely transplant referral.

title: The Coding and Non-Coding Genomic Landscape of Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Etiological Risk Factors and their Current Clinical Implications.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common liver malignancy and a leading cause of cancer mortality, with burden projected to rise substantially by 2040. Its poor prognosis reflects the timing of diagnosis: HCC develops silently against chronic liver disease, and six-monthly ultrasound with alpha-fetoprotein remains insensitive in the early stages. Two developments have reshaped molecular understanding of this heterogeneous cancer. Large-scale sequencing established that the somatic landscape is not etiology-agnostic. The driver hierarchy is dominated by TERT, TP53, and CTNNB1; exposure-specific mutational signatures; and structural events such as hepatitis B virus integration, all of which differ systematically by upstream cause. In parallel, a dense non-coding regulatory layer has been shown to intersect with the core processes of hepatocarcinogenesis. These layers have largely been reviewed in isolation. Here, we integrate them, organize the coding and non-coding genomic architecture of HCC by etiological risk factor, and appraise the contributions of each to clinical decision-making. Etiological patterning is asymmetric - well-established at the coding layer but not yet demonstrated at the non-coding layer, where assignments derive from single-etiology cohorts compared across studies, platforms, and normalization strategies. Cutting across both layers are convergent nodes shared by all causes, most clearly depletion of the hepatoprotective microRNA-122, a marker of convergence rather than specificity. We then assess the clinical interface: multi-analyte serum scores and methylation-based cell-free DNA now outperform ultrasound for early detection in prospective cohorts, yet none is guideline-endorsed, and no circulating non-coding RNA has reached prospective validation. The near-term clinical yield of this field lies in risk stratification, not molecularly guided therapy.
journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD
